Sandbox_RoadOpenedEngineDoorChance_toolt: Chance of an open hood (engine cover) at a car that appeared on the road or in a traffic jam.
Sandbox_RoadOpenedTrunkDoorChance: Chance of an open trunk on the road
Sandbox_RoadOpenedTrunkDoorChance_toolti: Chance of an open trunk at a car that appeared on the road or in a traffic jam.
Sandbox_RoadOpenedWindowChance: Chance of an open window on the road
Sandbox_RoadOpenedWindowChance_tooltip: Chance of an open window at a car that appeared on the road or in a traffic jam.
Sandbox_RoleplaySupporterIcons4219MP_RPC: Maximum distance in tiles at which another RP Mode player can receive /ic chat. The default of 30 matches local /say range.
Sandbox_RollBackRainCollectorBarrel_Pass: Currently, in version 42, water in rain barrel is updated only while it is raining <LINE>If you move to a region with rain barrel after the rain has stopped in another area, <LINE>the water that should have accumulated during the rain will not update and will instead be updated all at once the next time it rains. Enabling this option fixes this issue. <LINE>However, as the status of rain barrel is checked every 10 minutes, there may be slight frame drops depending on the number of rain barrels
Sandbox_RollBackRainCollectorBarrel_Snow: Allow snow to fill the rain collector barrel
Sandbox_Roll_ExtinguishFireChances_toolt: Chances to remove the fire on character with each roll. <LINE>0 -> never <LINE>100 -> always
Sandbox_RoofClimbFallDamage: Roof Climb: take fall damage when jumping down
Sandbox_RoofClimbFallDamage_tooltip: When ON, jumping straight down from a tall vehicle roof can scratch ankles or fracture a leg. When OFF, dismounts are always safe. Default ON.
Sandbox_RoofClimbPeerVisualSync_tooltip: Experimental MP visual fix. When ON, players standing on the same vehicle roof render each other at roof height. No server teleport is used. Default OFF.
Sandbox_RoofClimbStrengthRequired_toolti: Minimum Strength skill required to climb onto a normal car or sedan. Range 0-10. Default 3.
Sandbox_RoofClimbTallStrengthRequired_to: Minimum Strength required to climb onto vans, pickups, step vans and military trucks. Range 0-10. Default 5.
Sandbox_RoofClimbZombieVisibility: Roof Climb: zombie sight %% while on roof
Sandbox_RoofClimbZombieVisibility_toolti: Roughly how visible the player is to zombies while standing on a vehicle roof. 100 = same as ground. Lower values let you scout safely. Range 0-100. Default 50.
Sandbox_RooftopAnimalSafety_DisableAnima: When enabled, animals flee instead of starting stress attacks or retaliating against players. Vanilla shares its retaliation flag with zombie attackers, so animals will not retaliate against zombies either. Reload the save after changing this option.
Sandbox_RooftopAnimalSafety_DisableHeigh: When enabled, elevated animals receive vanilla height stress even inside a complete solid fence or wall enclosure.
Sandbox_RooftopAnimalSafety_FenceIndestr: Animal protection disables building attacks for all animals. Animal-only mode leaves mod-built boundaries vulnerable to zombies; animal-and-zombie mode also protects those boundaries from zombies. Players can still dismantle them. Reload the save after changing modes so animal definitions refresh.
Sandbox_RotDelay_tooltip:
How many rot checks a mature crop survives before finally rotting.
0 = Never rot (default); N = rots after N postponed checks
Sandbox_RouletteRealDeath_tooltip: When ON, a lethal Russian Roulette outcome is applied by the server as a real character death. When OFF, the session keeps its existing cinematic outcome behavior. Default OFF.
Sandbox_RouletteRerollEachLap: Roulette - reroll kill chamber each lap
Sandbox_RouletteRerollEachLap_tooltip: When ON, the hidden kill chamber is re-rolled at the start of every full circle of pulls. Default OFF keeps the same chamber for the entire session.
Sandbox_RubberFabric_MinConditionToRepai: Item must be at least this condition (0–1) to be eligible for repair. Set 0.0 to allow repairing from broken state.
Sandbox_RubberFabric_RequiredLevelToRepa: Minimum tailoring level required to repair rubber items (0–10).
Sandbox_RubberFabric_T_CanRepairRubber_t: If enabled, the Electric Sewing machine can repair rubber items or rubberized sections.
Sandbox_SCP.AdrenalSurgeLootChance: Chance for Adrenal Surge Injector loot
Sandbox_SCP.AdrenalSurgeLootChance_toolt: Percentual chance for Adrenal Surge injectors to be dropped by zombies.
Sandbox_SCP.EmptyInjectorLootChance_tool: Percentual chance for Empty injectors to be dropped by zombies.
Sandbox_SCP.EnableInjectorZombieDrops_to: When enabled, zombies have a chance to drop empty injectors. These can be refilled with SCP serums for various effects.
Sandbox_SCP.HemovitaLootChance_tooltip: Percentual chance for Hemovita injectors to be dropped by zombies.
Sandbox_SCP.SCPDClassSpawnChance_tooltip: Percentual spawn chance. This value is shared with other outfit groups, meaning that at 100%% you will not exclusively spawn this outfit.
Sandbox_SCP.SCPDClassSurvivorSpawnChance: A D-Class subject that escaped during a containment breach. May possess limited SCP equipment before succumbing to the infected. Percentual spawn chance shared with other outfit groups; at 100%% you will not exclusively spawn this outfit.
Sandbox_SCP.SCPGuardSpawnChance_tooltip: Percentual spawn chance. This value is shared with other outfit groups, meaning that at 100%% you will not exclusively spawn this outfit.
Sandbox_SCP.SCPMTFBreacherSpawnChance_to: Percentual spawn chance. This value is shared with other outfit groups, meaning that at 100%% you will not exclusively spawn this outfit.
Sandbox_SCP.SCPMTFRangerSpawnChance_tool: Percentual spawn chance. This value is shared with other outfit groups, meaning that at 100%% you will not exclusively spawn this outfit.
Sandbox_SCP.SCPScientistSpawnChance_tool: Percentual spawn chance. This value is shared with other outfit groups, meaning that at 100%% you will not exclusively spawn this outfit.
Sandbox_SC_CooldownMinutes_tooltip: Minutes before the same stretch group or massage body part can be used again. 0 = no cooldown.
Sandbox_SC_EffectMultiplier_tooltip: Scales all stress, pain, and stiffness reductions. 100 = normal, 50 = half effect, 200 = double effect.
Sandbox_SC_FirstAidScaling_tooltip: When enabled, First Aid skill improves massage pain reduction (+1 per skill level).
Sandbox_SC_PainThreshold_tooltip: Minimum pain level before massage appears in the context menu. 0 = always available, 10 = default.
Sandbox_SC_SprainChance_tooltip: Chance of worsening pain when massaging a fractured body part. 0 = no risk, 15 = default, 100 = guaranteed.
Sandbox_SD_SpawnChance_tooltip: Common:1.5x, Uncommon:1.0x, Rare:0.5x, Very Rare:0.25x, default value is 1x
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_AlertAtScreamPosition_: Enabled: zombies walk toward where the scream actually happened (the sprinter's position) — tactically coherent with what you hear. Disabled: v1.0 legacy behavior, the horde converges on YOUR position.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_AlertNearbyZombies_too: If enabled, the scream uses the game’s sound system to alert zombies within a set radius. If disabled, the scream is only aesthetic — it scares the player but doesn’t affect horde AI. Great for immersive sound without changing difficulty.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_AlertRadius_tooltip: The size of the area, in tiles, where zombies will hear the scream and walk toward the source. Example: 20 affects just the nearby street; 80–100 can wake up half the neighborhood. Very high values make every scream a mini-horde event.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ChaseCooldownHours_too: Minimum in-game hours between screams from the SAME sprinter during a chase. 0.01 ≈ about 36 in-game seconds. Higher values make chases quieter; lower ones make them louder and more frantic.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ChaseScreechChance_too: Extra chance for a scream while the sprinter is already chasing you. Use low values (5–20) for occasional screams and higher ones for chaotic, noisy pursuits. Combine this with the cooldown setting to avoid endless screaming.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ClusterCooldownHours_t: Duration of the time window controlling screams per group (cluster), in in-game hours. Within this window, the total number of screams is limited by 'Max screams per group'. Example: 0.01 ≈ about 36 in-game seconds for that area.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ClusterRadius_tooltip: Defines the size of the area considered a single screaming scene. If multiple sprinters are within this radius, they count as one group (cluster). The scream limit per group applies to all of them, preventing endless chaos in crowded areas.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_EnableNearScream_toolt: When enabled, the sprinter emits an extra scream when entering close range (face scream), in addition to the discovery and chase screams. Disabling it reduces audio chaos in melee combat and keeps the mod cleaner in dense hordes.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_FarRange_tooltip: Maximum distance in tiles at which the discovery scream can be heard in 3D. Higher values make the sound travel farther, warning you of sprinters before you see them. Useful in open maps where echoes enhance immersion.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_FarVolume_tooltip: Controls the volume of the discovery scream when the sprinter is still far away. Example: 0.1 gives a faint echo; values near 1.0 make the scream stand out even from a distance.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_GlobalVolume_tooltip: General volume multiplier applied to all screams in the mod. 1.0 = default; 0.5 = half volume; 2.0 = double volume (careful with your ears). Use this to balance the mod’s audio with the rest of the game.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_MaxClusterScreams_tool: Maximum number of screams allowed in each group during the set window. Example: with value 2, even if 10 sprinters spot you at once, only 2 screams will be heard in that scene.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_MaxProcessDistance_too: Maximum distance in tiles from the player within which theySEE YOU still processes sprinters for screams. Zombies beyond this radius are ignored to save performance. Values between 180 and 250 maintain immersion while staying efficient.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_MaxScreamsPerChapter_t: Scream limit for each chapter of a hunt. A chapter resets when the sprinter loses you and finds you again, so long chases stay alive instead of going permanently silent (v1.0 behavior). Example: 4 allows discovery + face scream + two chase screams per chapter.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_NearAsWorldSound_toolt: If enabled, the close scream uses PlayWorldSound just like the distant one — full 3D sound with spatial direction and echo, perfect for headsets. If disabled, it uses the zombie’s local audio, sharper and more direct.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_NearVolume_tooltip: Volume multiplier when the sprinter screams right in your face. For a stronger jump scare, use 1.0 or higher; high values make screams much more aggressive.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_PitchVariation_tooltip: Each sprinter rolls a personal voice pitch within this range and keeps it for life, so the same voice bank produces thousands of distinct hunters. 0 disables it (all voices identical); 7 gives clearly distinct voices while staying natural.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_RediscoveryHours_toolt: How long (in in-game hours) a sprinter must lose sight of you before its discovery scream re-arms. When it spots you again, a new hunt chapter begins — expect a fresh 'FOUND YOU' scream. 0.04 = a few real seconds; higher values make rediscoveries rarer and more dramatic.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ScreechChance_tooltip: Probability that a sprinter will let out a discovery scream the first time they see you. 0 = never screams; 100 = almost every sprinter screams as soon as they spot you. Example: 60 means roughly 6 out of 10 encounters start with a scream.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ShoutResponseRadius_to: Maximum distance at which a sprinter can hear and answer your shout. 50 covers the surrounding streets; higher values let the whole neighborhood answer.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ShoutResponse_tooltip: When you shout, up to two nearby sprinters scream back after a short beat — call and response. They reveal their position and voice before you ever see them.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_TickRate_tooltip: How many ticks the game waits before reprocessing each sprinter. Lower values = faster reaction but more CPU load; higher = lighter but slower. 6 is a recommended balance for large hordes and helicopter events.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_TimeMode_tooltip: Defines at what time of day sprinters can use their special scream. 0 = day and night; 1 = day only; 2 = night only. Example: use '2' for calmer days and much more tense nights.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_AlertAtScreamPo: Kept only so old presets load. A confirmed world sound always starts at the sprinter's real position and floor; this value has no effect.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_AlertNearbyZomb: After a scream is confirmed, one vanilla world sound starts at the sprinter's real position. Any zombie type inside the radius may react. Disable for audio only.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_AlertRadius_too: Hearing radius for normal zombies and sprinters. This works only when attraction is enabled; larger values can move a larger horde.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_ChaseCooldownHo: Interval between chase-scream attempts for the same sprinter. 0.03 = 108 in-game seconds. Lower values are more vocal; real time follows day length.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_ChaseScreechCha: One roll is made per eligible chase interval. 0 disables chase screams; 100 makes every eligible interval succeed. Identification is always guaranteed on target lock.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_ClusterCooldown: How long confirmed screams remain in the nearby-area budget. 0.01 = 36 in-game seconds; real time follows day length.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_ClusterRadius_t: Nearby confirmed screams share an area budget. Larger values suppress more overlapping follow-up screams. The target-lock identification scream bypasses this limit.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_EnableNearScrea: Allows an extra scream when a sprinter enters within 8 tiles after being farther away. Disable it to reduce noise during close combat.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_EnablePresenceS: Allows sprinters without a locked target to scream occasionally while a player is within the encounter range. Disable it to keep only screams tied to target lock, the hunt, close range or a player shout.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_FarRange_toolti: Spontaneous presence screams and target-locked hunt screams can occur only while a player is within this distance. The full 10-300 tile range is supported.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_FarVolume_toolt: Controls every scream except the close-range scream. 0.08 is recommended; 0.10 is normal level; values above 0.10 progressively amplify it up to 3x.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_GlobalVolume_to: Multiplier applied to every mod voice. 1.0 keeps the intended mix; lower values soften it and higher values amplify it.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_MaxClusterScrea: Number of confirmed screams the area can hold before follow-up screams are suppressed. Identification screams still occur, then quiet later screams nearby.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_MaxProcessDista: Limits how far away target-locked sprinters are fully evaluated. Spontaneous voices use the vocal range, so that range becomes the minimum automatically. Higher values may use more CPU.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_MaxScreamsPerCh: Maximum confirmed screams in one hunt chapter. Identification or rediscovery starts a chapter; after 0.1 in-game hour, a silent sprinter can gain a second wind.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_NearAsWorldSoun: Kept only so old presets load. Every scream now plays from the actual sprinter's moving 3D source; this value has no effect.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_NearVolume_tool: Volume multiplier used only for close-range screams. 1.0 is normal; lower values soften them and higher values make them louder.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_PitchVariation_: Maximum pitch offset assigned from each sprinter's stable identity. 0 keeps the source pitch; 7 allows up to +/-7%%. The same sprinter keeps its voice and pitch.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_PresenceScreamC: Chance of a distant presence scream (%%)
Rolled once whenever a distant presence scream becomes eligible. 0 prevents it; 100 preserves the original frequency. A failed roll waits for a new normal interval. Other scream types are unaffected.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_RediscoveryHour: Time without the target or clear sight before a rediscovery scream can occur. 0.04 = 144 in-game seconds; real time follows day length.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_ScreechChance_t: Kept only so old presets load. Identification occurs when a sprinter locks a player as its chase target; this value has no effect.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_ShoutResponse: Allow sprinters to answer player shouts
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_ShoutResponseRa: Maximum distance for an eligible sprinter to answer. This works only when shout responses are enabled; area limits may reduce the number of replies.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_ShoutResponse_t: A real player shout has only a limited chance of an answer, and at most one eligible sprinter responds. After answering, it stays silent for 0.4 in-game hour; repeated shouts cannot force replies.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_TickRate_toolti: Lower values react sooner and use more CPU; higher values spread the work and react later. 6 is recommended. Timing does not depend on frame rate.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TheySEEyou_TimeMode_toolti: 0 = anytime; 1 = day and brighter twilight; 2 = night and darker twilight. Dawn and dusk change gradually.
Sandbox_SN_BaseZombieCount_tooltip: How many zombies attack on your very first siege. Later sieges grow bigger based on the Growth Rate setting below. Example: 50 means about 50 zombies on siege #1.
Sandbox_SN_BreakerPercent_tooltip: The chance each zombie has to be a Breaker (wall smasher). 10%% means roughly 1 in 10 zombies will be a breaker. Breakers wear construction gear and destroy barricades and walls faster than normal. Set to 0 to disable breakers.
Sandbox_SN_DirectionalAttacks_tooltip: When ON, zombies mostly attack from one direction each siege (North, South, East, or West). The direction is announced when the siege starts. Makes defending your base more strategic since you know which wall to fortify.
Sandbox_SN_Enabled_tooltip: Master switch. Turn this OFF to completely disable all siege events.
Sandbox_SN_FirstSiegeDay_tooltip: Which in-game day the very first siege happens. Example: 5 means your first siege is on Day 5.
Sandbox_SN_FrequencyDaysMax_tooltip: The most days between siege nights. Leave at 0 to always use the Min value exactly (no randomness). Set higher than Min for unpredictable timing. Example: Min=3, Max=7 means a siege every 3 to 7 days.
Sandbox_SN_FrequencyDays_tooltip: The fewest days between siege nights. Example: 5 means at least 5 days between each siege. If you also set the Max value above 0, the gap will be random between Min and Max.
Sandbox_SN_MaxActiveZombies_tooltip: The most siege zombies that can be alive at the same time. When this limit is reached, new zombies stop spawning until you kill some. Lower values = smoother performance and steadier action. Higher values = more overwhelming but can cause lag. Default: 400. If your game stutters during sieges, try lowering this.
Sandbox_SN_MaxZombies_tooltip: The absolute maximum number of zombies that can appear in a single siege night, no matter how far you've progressed. Once this many have spawned, the siege is over. Think of this as the siege length cap. Example: 800 means the siege ends after 800 zombies total.
Sandbox_SN_MiniHorde_ActivityScaling_too: When ON, mini-hordes are bigger when you've been busy (killing zombies, shooting, running generators). If you've been quiet, mini-hordes are smaller.
Sandbox_SN_MiniHorde_CooldownMinutes_too: How many in-game minutes must pass after a mini-horde before another one can trigger. Prevents back-to-back attacks. Default: 60 minutes.
Sandbox_SN_MiniHorde_Enabled_tooltip: Adds small zombie attacks between siege nights, triggered by noise you make. Running generators, firing guns, driving vehicles, and being generally loud can attract nearby zombies to your location. Disabled by default.
Sandbox_SN_MiniHorde_EstablishmentScalin: When ON, the more built-up your base is (generators, loot, defenses), the bigger your sieges and mini-hordes become. Building a bigger base attracts more attention.
Sandbox_SN_MiniHorde_MaxPerDay_tooltip: The most mini-hordes that can happen in one in-game day. Resets at midnight. Set to 0 for no daily limit. Default: 2.
Sandbox_SN_MiniHorde_MaxZombies_tooltip: Maximum zombies in one mini-horde (at maximum noise). Default: 35.
Sandbox_SN_MiniHorde_MinZombies_tooltip: Minimum zombies in a mini-horde (at threshold noise). Default: 8.
Sandbox_SN_MiniHorde_NoiseThreshold_tool: How much noise you need to make before a mini-horde shows up. Lower numbers = mini-hordes come more easily (even quiet activity triggers them). Higher numbers = only very loud activities like gunfire and vehicle crashes attract them. Default: 100.
Sandbox_SN_MiniHorde_PlayerScaling_toolt: Multiplayer only. When ON, more online players means bigger mini-hordes.
Sandbox_SN_SafehouseMergeDistance_toolti: Only matters when Zombie Target is set to Safehouse. If two safehouses are closer together than this distance, they're treated as one target. Prevents zombies from awkwardly splitting between buildings that are right next to each other. Default: 50.
Sandbox_SN_SafehouseSearchRadius_tooltip: Only matters when Zombie Target is set to Safehouse. How far away the mod looks for your claimed safehouse. If your base isn't being targeted during sieges, try increasing this. Default: 300.
Sandbox_SN_ScalingMultiplier_tooltip: How much harder each siege gets compared to the last. At 1.5: Siege 1 = 50 zombies, Siege 2 = 75, Siege 3 = 112, Siege 4 = 168, and so on. Set to 1.0 if you want every siege to stay the same size. In multiplayer, more players also means more zombies.
Sandbox_SN_SharedSpawnRadius_tooltip: Multiplayer only. Players within this distance of each other fight the SAME siege together. If players are farther apart than this, each group gets their own separate siege. Default: 200. Increase if your group is spread across a large compound.
Sandbox_SN_SiegeEndHour_tooltip: What hour the siege ends and any remaining zombies are cleared, using 24-hour time. Default: 6 (6:00 AM). The siege can also end early if you kill all the zombies before this time.
Sandbox_SN_SiegeMode_option1: Per-Base: Each player group fights their own siege
Sandbox_SN_SiegeMode_option2: Unified: Everyone shares one big siege
Sandbox_SN_SiegeMode_tooltip: How sieges work in multiplayer. Per-Base: each group of nearby players fights their own independent siege with separate waves and kills. Unified: ALL players share one global siege — waves, kills, and progress are combined. The unified siege targets wherever the most players and infrastructure are concentrated.
Sandbox_SN_SiegeStartHour_tooltip: What hour the siege begins, using 24-hour time. Default: 20 (8:00 PM). Set to 22 for a late-night start, or 18 for early evening.
Sandbox_SN_SiegeWeatherEnabled_tooltip: Adds spooky weather during siege nights — fog rolls in before the siege, rain and wind pick up during combat, and everything clears at dawn. This is purely visual and does NOT affect gameplay difficulty.
Sandbox_SN_SiegeWeatherIntensity_tooltip: How dramatic the weather effects are. 1.0 = normal. 0.5 = subtle effects. 2.0 = thick fog and heavy rain. Set to 0 to effectively disable weather without turning off the setting above.
Sandbox_SN_SpawnAnchor_option1: Players: Zombies chase you wherever you go
Sandbox_SN_SpawnAnchor_option2: Safehouse: Zombies attack your claimed base, even if you leave
Sandbox_SN_SpawnAnchor_tooltip: What zombies focus on during a siege.
Sandbox_SN_SpawnDistance_tooltip: How far from your position zombies appear when the siege starts. Higher values give you more time to see them coming. If you have a large base, increase this so zombies don't appear inside your walls. Default: 45. Most bases work well between 40-60.
Sandbox_SN_SpecialZombiesEnabled_tooltip: Adds tougher zombie types to siege nights: Sprinters (fast runners), Breakers (smash through walls), and Tanks (huge and hard to kill). These spawn mixed in with regular zombies.
Sandbox_SN_SpecialZombiesStartWeek_toolt: Which siege number special zombies start appearing. Example: 3 means your first two sieges are normal zombies only, and specials show up starting on siege #3. Gives new players time to get ready.
Sandbox_SN_SprinterPercent_tooltip: The chance each zombie has to be a Sprinter (fast runner). 5%% means roughly 1 in 20 zombies will sprint at you. Sprinters look like regular zombies but move much faster. Set to 0 to disable sprinters.
Sandbox_SN_StripSiegeZombieLoot_tooltip: Removes extra items from siege zombies (they keep their clothes). Turn this ON if siege zombies are dropping too much loot, especially if you have mods that add items to zombie inventories.
Sandbox_SN_TankCount_tooltip: How many Tank zombies appear each siege night. Tanks wear military gear, move slowly, but take many hits to kill. They show up during the last third of the night. Set to 0 to disable tanks.
Sandbox_SN_TankHealthMultiplier_tooltip: How many times tougher a Tank is compared to a regular zombie. At 5.0, a Tank takes about 5 times as many hits to kill. Increase for a real bullet sponge, decrease if tanks feel impossible.
Sandbox_SN_WarningSignsEnabled_tooltip: When ON, your character will mutter and you'll hear distant sounds during the day before a siege night. This gives you time to prepare and get back to base.
Sandbox_SN_WaveBreakSeconds_tooltip: How long (in seconds) the longest pause between attack waves can be. Leave at 0 for automatic pacing (5-12 seconds between waves). Set a specific number to cap it, e.g. 5 means waves always come within 5 seconds. Note: zombies still trickle in during pauses.
Sandbox_SOS_AmmoPercent_tooltip: 100%% is the normal kit. 50%% gives half of each ammo stack; 200%% doubles it; 0%% removes loadout ammo.
Sandbox_SOS_BreachNoisePercent_tooltip: 100%% is normal: 12-tile attraction radius. 50%% is 6 tiles. 200%% is 24 tiles. 0%% creates no zombie-attraction sound.
Sandbox_SOS_BreachSeconds_tooltip: Set 0 to disable breach charges. Standard placement time is 12 seconds.
Sandbox_SOS_CombatAbilityPercent_tooltip: 100%% is normal. 50%% halves numerical combat effects, such as the One Shot bonus (2.0 damage becomes 1.0). 150%% makes them 1.5 times stronger. 0%% disables scripted combat abilities.
Sandbox_SOS_CombatRecoveryPercent_toolti: Scales SOS combat recovery effects. 100%% is normal, 50%% halves them, 200%% doubles them, and 0%% disables them.
Sandbox_SOS_DeadOperatorCount_tooltip: Number of lootable dead operators seeded in a newly created world. Set 0 to disable.
Sandbox_SOS_DropzoneEnabled_tooltip: Adds the military-approach spawn option to character creation.
Sandbox_SOS_EnduranceResistancePercent_t: Reduces new incoming Endurance loss for Operators; it does not restore Endurance. 35%% is standard, 0%% gives no reduction, and 75%% gives the maximum reduction.
Sandbox_SOS_FatigueResistancePercent_too: Reduces new incoming Fatigue gain for Operators; it does not remove existing Fatigue. 30%% is standard, 0%% gives no reduction, and 65%% gives the maximum reduction.
Sandbox_SOS_GhostStealthRange_tooltip: Range in which Ghost night cloak can break zombie targeting. Standard is 14 tiles. Set 0 to turn it off.
Sandbox_SOS_MedicHealingPercent_tooltip: 100%% is normal. 50%% halves every scripted SOS healing amount. 150%% increases it by half. 0%% disables scripted SOS healing.
Sandbox_SOS_MedicSupplyUsePercent_toolti: Scales medical supplies consumed by Combat Medic effects. 100%% is normal, 50%% uses half as much, and 200%% uses twice as much.
Sandbox_SOS_MedicTreatmentPercent_toolti: Scales Combat Medic treatment effects. 100%% is normal, 50%% halves them, 200%% doubles them, and 0%% disables them.
Sandbox_SOS_MedicalSupplyPercent_tooltip: 100%% is the normal kit. 50%% gives half of each medical stack; 200%% doubles it; 0%% removes medical supplies.
Sandbox_SOS_PainResistancePercent_toolti: Reduces new incoming Pain gain for Operators; it does not remove existing Pain or heal wounds. 35%% is standard, 0%% gives no reduction, and 75%% gives the maximum reduction.
Sandbox_SOS_ProfessionGrantsPoints_toolt: Enabled: 14 means +14 points to spend (the original mod behavior). Disabled: 14 means -14 points to spend (a 14-point cost).
Sandbox_SOS_ProfessionPointValue_tooltip: Magnitude of the profession's point effect. The direction is set by the option below.
Sandbox_SOS_ScoutSenseRange_tooltip: Range in which Scout Sense marks zombies while sneaking. Standard is 18 tiles. Set 0 to turn it off.
Sandbox_SOS_SquadAuraRange_tooltip: Range of the Squad Leader's panic suppression and non-stacking incoming Endurance-loss resistance. It never restores Endurance or health. Standard is 14 tiles; set 0 to turn it off.
Sandbox_SOS_StartingKitLevel_tooltip: 0 = civilian character preview; a selected Loadout trait replaces it with its complete paid SOS package. 1 = basic clothing and survival items. 2 = standard SOS kit. 3 = reinforced kit with extra supplies.
Sandbox_SOS_SuppressorReductionPercent_t: 75%% is the default: a 100-tile gunshot becomes 25 tiles. 50%% halves it. 0%% gives no sound reduction. 95%% is near silent.
Sandbox_SOTO_AddFitXPWhileRun_tooltip: Player can earn additional Fitness XP once per game minute while running.
Sandbox_SOTO_AgilityTraitsObtainable_too:
Possibility to obtain XP boosts while leveling agility skills.
For example, player can obtain Sneaky trait to increase their XP gain for Sneaking skill.
Sandbox_SOTO_AlcoholicHoursToRemoveMax: Max. hours to remove Alcoholic trait:
Sandbox_SOTO_AlcoholicHoursToRemoveMax_t: Should be higher than Min. 1 day = 24
Sandbox_SOTO_AlcoholicHoursToRemoveMin: Min. hours to remove Alcoholic trait:
Sandbox_SOTO_AlcoholicHoursToRemoveMin_t: Should be lower than Max. 1 day = 24
Sandbox_SOTO_AlcoholicValueToEarnMax: Max. value to earn Alcoholic trait:
Sandbox_SOTO_AlcoholicValueToEarnMax_too: Should be higher than Min. 1 alcohol bottle = ~300
Sandbox_SOTO_AlcoholicValueToEarnMin: Min. value to earn Alcoholic trait:
Sandbox_SOTO_AlcoholicValueToEarnMin_too: Should be lower than Max. 1 alcohol bottle = ~300

Sandbox_SaucedCarts_EnableCorpseStorage_: EXPERIMENTAL — off by default. Allows loading and unloading corpses to/from carts via grapple + right-click 'Load into Cart'. Includes vanilla-faithful rot accounting (corpses age in the cart, despawn at the sandbox HoursForCorpseRemoval threshold). Still being tested in MP — opt in if you want to try it; expect rough edges.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_EnableDebugLogs_tool: Enable detailed debug logging. Disable for better performance when playing with PZ debug mode on.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_EnableMod_tooltip: Enable or disable the SaucedCarts mod.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_LoadedCartSpawns_too: EXPERIMENTAL — off by default. How often a spawned cart comes pre-loaded with loot that fits where it spawned — groceries outside homes and lots, materials/tools in warehouses and stores, and (very rarely) a survivor's cache of weapons and ammo. Most carts stay empty, so a loaded one is a find. Still being tested — opt in if you want to try it; expect rough edges. Off = always empty (default).
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_MaintenanceSkillBonu: When enabled, Maintenance skill improves repair effectiveness and speed, and awards XP.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_MaxCartsPerBuilding_: Maximum number of carts that can spawn in a single building. 1 = default, 5 = max.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_OutdoorSpawnDensity_: How often carts spawn outdoors in vehicle zones — store parking lots, residential driveways, and trailer-park parking (the same map zones that spawn cars), like an abandoned 'escaped cart'. Off = indoors only. Scales with Spawn Rate.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_ProtectFromWorldClea: Only matters on servers that run world cleanup in keep-list mode (ItemRemovalListBlacklistToggle enabled), where every item type not on the WorldItemRemovalList is deleted at chunk load — including carts left on the ground with all their cargo. When this option is enabled, SaucedCarts adds its cart types to that list in memory at every boot so cleanup can never delete a cart. Off by default because it changes how your cleanup list behaves; nothing is ever written to your config files.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_RepairAmountMultipli: How much condition is restored per repair. 100 = default, 200 = double repair, 50 = half repair.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_RepairTimeMultiplier: How long repairs take. 100 = default, 50 = faster repairs, 200 = slower repairs.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_SpawnRate_tooltip: How often carts spawn in the world. 100 = default, 0 = no spawns, 200 = double spawns.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_SpeedPenaltyMultipli: Movement speed penalty while pushing a cart. 100 = default (slightly slower run), 0 = no penalty, 500 = five times the penalty. High values make pushers too slow to sprint, which also disables the stand-on-and-ride sprint animation.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_StrictShopOnly_toolt: When enabled, carts only spawn in buildings PZ flags as shops (BuildingDef.isShop). Reduces surprise spawns at the cost of some legitimate spawn locations. Combined with the always-on residential/outdoor filter.
Sandbox_SaucedCarts_WeightReduction_tool: Percentage of item weight reduced when stored in carts. 95 = items weigh 5%% of normal (default), 100 = items weigh nothing, 0 = no reduction.
Sandbox_ScavengingSkill_MultiplierConfig: Rate at which Scavenging skill levels up. (Global Multiplier must be unchecked)

Multiplies the chance of student zombies appearing in the general (default) zombie population. Increase this to see more student zombies outside school.
This is a MULTIPLIER, not a percentage: some normal zombies will still appear, even with high values. Location-specific zombies (e.g., prisoner zombies) are unaffected.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_GenderRatio_tooltip:
Ratio of males to females among student zombies.
This only applies to zombies in schools; student zombies spawned in the default pool will be 50/50.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_GymsuitStyle_tooltip: The style of gym uniform worn by student zombies. Boys will wear shorts instead of skirts/bloomers.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_RibbonColor_tooltip:
The color tie worn by student zombies.
NyanCat's Blazer does not support modular ribbons; zombies wearing it ignore this option.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_RibbonStyleBlazer_too:
The tie worn by female student zombies with blazers and sweaters.
Men always wear neckties. Zombies wearing NyanCat's Blazer ignore this option.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_RibbonStyleSailor_too: The tie worn by student zombies with sailor suits.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_SailorColor_tooltip:
The color/style sailor suit worn by student zombies, if/when they wear them.
Options are in shirt / collar format, e.g. White / Black is white with a black collar.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_SeifukuStyle_tooltip: The style of uniform worn by student zombies.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_SpawnChanceModifier_t:
School's Out item spawn chances are multiplied by this number, modifying their chance of appearing in the world.
Change this if you feel like uniform components appear too frequently or not enough.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_SpawnChanceToggle_too: School's Out items will spawn in world containers like lockers, dressers, etc.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_SweaterColor_tooltip: The color sweater worn by student zombies, if/when they wear them.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_SwimsuitStyle_tooltip:
The style of swimsuit worn by female student zombies. New type sukumizu have a higher cut than the old type.
This also affects item rarity: non-approved sukumizu types will be harder to find.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_UseSeifukuZombies_too:
Student zombies in schools, etc. will wear Japanese-style student uniforms.
Deselect this to spawn vanilla student zombies instead.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_UseVanillaZombies_too:
Japanese-style student zombies will spawn alongside vanilla student zombies.
Requires Dress Code Enforced.
Sandbox_SchoolsOut_WhiteSwimsuitToggle_t:
Female student swimmers will wear white sukumizu instead of blue.
This also affects item rarity: sukumizu in non-approved colors will be harder to find.
Sandbox_ScrapSurvival_RecyclingYieldMult: Controls how many materials are recovered when recycling. 1.00 = normal yield, 0.50 = half yield, 2.00 = double yield. Item condition and the character’s relevant skill still influence the final result.
Sandbox_ScrapSurvival_SkillRequirements_: Yes: Salvage Works recipes use their intended skill levels. No: skill levels do not block mod recipes. Materials, tools and workstations are still required. This option is applied when the world/server is loaded; after changing it during a running game, reload the save or reconnect before testing recipes.
Sandbox_SearchInteractionMode_tooltip: Choose whether searching skips animation or first walks to the container and plays the loot animation.
Sandbox_SearchNoiseInterval_tooltip: Seconds between noise pulses while searching.
Sandbox_SearchNoiseReductionMode_tooltip: Controls whether Dextrous and/or Sneaking skill reduce the zombie-attraction radius created while searching. This changes the world sound radius, not the sound effect volume heard by players.
Sandbox_SearchNoiseVolume_tooltip: World sound volume for normal searching.
Sandbox_SearchRefocusDuration_tooltip: How long, in milliseconds, the loot window should keep the searched container selected when a search action starts. 0 disables this refocus. Higher values may help if nearby containers make the tab jump during turning or animation.
Sandbox_SearchSoundVolumeMultiplier_tool: Multiplies the actual search sound effect volume heard by players during normal searching. Does not affect zombie-attraction noise.
Sandbox_SearchTimeMultiplier_tooltip: Multiplies the time required to search a container. Higher values make searching slower.
Sandbox_SearchXPMultiplier_tooltip: Multiplies XP gained from revealing loot. Default 1 keeps rewards much lower than regular foraging pickups.
Sandbox_SeasonalMoods_Autumn_tooltip: ON (default): autumn gets its faded amber / sepia grade. OFF: autumn stays vanilla.
Sandbox_SeasonalMoods_Fog_tooltip: OFF (default): colour and desaturation only - no extra haze. ON: summer gets a faint heat haze and winter a light fog on top of the normal weather. Atmospheric, but it does add visible fog the base game wouldn't have, and it very slightly softens distant visibility.
Sandbox_SeasonalMoods_Intensity_tooltip: The STARTING strength of the colour grade (0-100%%) for a new world - after that, adjust it live in-game with the on-screen box (default key F7). 0 = off (pure vanilla), 70 = default, 100 = the full cinematic look. The grade is cosmetic - it tints the picture and drains colour but never changes how far you can see.
Sandbox_SeasonalMoods_Spring_tooltip: ON (default): spring gets its fresh green grade. OFF: spring stays vanilla.
Sandbox_SeasonalMoods_Summer_tooltip: ON (default): summer gets its warm golden, slightly hazy grade. OFF: summer stays vanilla.
Sandbox_SeasonalMoods_Winter_tooltip: ON (default): winter gets its cold, bleached blue grade. OFF: winter stays vanilla.
Sandbox_SeeTarget_AnimalAmount_tooltip: Number of animal trailers spawned in the event, recommended only 1
Sandbox_SeeTarget_BagRewards_tooltip: Comma-separated list of items that will appear in zombie backpacks, Base.ID format
Sandbox_SeeTarget_CooldownHours_tooltip: Minimum time in hours between events to prevent them from spawning continuously
Sandbox_SeeTarget_Enable_tooltip: Enables or disables the global event system for all players
Sandbox_SeeTarget_EventDuration_tooltip: Duration in hours that the event remains active before disappearing
Sandbox_SeeTarget_LootContainerType_tool: Defines the items that appear inside the military container, separated by commas
Sandbox_SeeTarget_ShowHaloText_tooltip: Displays a visual message above the player when an event appears
Sandbox_SeeTarget_ShowServerMsg_tooltip: Displays a global server message when an event is generated
Sandbox_SeeTarget_SpawnAnimals_tooltip: Enables or disables events where animal trailers appear
Sandbox_SeeTarget_SpawnChancePerHour_too: Defines the hourly chance of a new map event spawning. If you want few events, use 1 or 2
Sandbox_SeeTarget_SpawnLootBox_tooltip: Enables or disables the event that spawns a military crate with loot. If nobody participates, the event is removed automatically
Sandbox_SeeTarget_SpawnVehicle_tooltip: Enables or disables events where vehicles appear
Sandbox_SeeTarget_SpawnZombies_tooltip: Enables or disables events where zombie hordes appear. If nobody participates, the event is removed automatically
Sandbox_SeeTarget_VehicleSpawnCount_tool: Number of vehicles spawned in the event, recommended 1, max 2
Sandbox_SeeTarget_VehicleSpawnWithKey_to: Defines whether vehicles spawn with a key in the glovebox
Sandbox_SeeTarget_ZombieAmount_tooltip: Number of zombies spawned in the event, recommended more than 30
Sandbox_SeinarSurvivalKit_KitLevel_toolt: Items your character spawns with. Basic gives a minimal loadout, Full gives the complete nomad kit.
Sandbox_ShelterHoldBeehive_EnableZombees: Allows Zombees to appear while foraging and when disassembling wild honeycombs. When disabled, existing Zombees are kept for save compatibility but cannot be inserted into a hive again after removal.
Sandbox_ShiftFastSearchMultiplier_toolti: Search speed multiplier while the fast-search key is held. 2 means twice as fast.
Sandbox_ShortBluntUpgradeCap_tooltip: For option 2 of Max Upgrade Handling - applies to Short Blunt category weapons
Sandbox_ShortSharpUpgradeCap_tooltip: For option 2 of Max Upgrade Handling - applies to Short Sharp category weapons
Sandbox_ShowCycleMessages_tooltip: When enable, player will speak about the cycle.
Sandbox_ShowDiscoveredPOIs_tooltip: Displays learned point-of-interest markers on the world map (M). Untick to hide all N3WO Map Overhaul markers.
Sandbox_ShowKeyOrigin_CompassNeeded: Compass is needed to show key origin
Sandbox_ShowKeyOrigin_CompassNeeded_tool: When enabled, key origin only will be shown if you have a compass in your inventory.
Sandbox_ShowPOIs_tooltip: Displays marked points of interest on the spawn-selection map. Untick to hide the POI button and all POI markers from players.
Sandbox_ShowSearchDebugTooltips_tooltip: Shows the next hidden stack's rarity and search cost in the search button tooltip. Disabled by default.
Sandbox_ShowSearchNoiseDebug_tooltip: When enabled, searching draws the normal or fast-search sound radius and flashes when a world sound pulse is created. Debug only; disabled by default.
Sandbox_ShowSearchXPNotification_tooltip: When enabled, gaining Foraging XP from searching uses the original floating XP notification. Disabled by default for immersion.
Sandbox_SignatureWeapons_AutoUnclaimOnDe: On death your claimed weapons revert to legacy weapons and free your claim slots.
Sandbox_SignatureWeapons_InfiniteSharpne: Claimed bladed weapons never dull. When off, signature weapons keep full durability but must be sharpened normally.
Sandbox_SignatureWeapons_MaxClaims_toolt: How many weapons you may have claimed at once.
Sandbox_SignatureWeapons_ProgressionRate: How fast claimed weapons level up (1:  normal / 2:  twice as fast).
Sandbox_SilencerDistribution_tooltip: Multiplies how often the factory Suppressor spawns in loot. 1.0 = default rate, 0 = never spawns in loot (admin/debug spawn only), up to 5x default.
Sandbox_SimpleLockpicking_ActionSpeedMul: Higher values will decrease the time it takes for the player to pick a lock.
Sandbox_SimpleLockpicking_BurglarBonus_t: Additional chance for the player to succeed a lockpick attempt if they are a burglar.
Sandbox_SimpleLockpicking_CanFailLockpic: Determines whether it is possible for the player to fail a lockpick attempt or not.
Sandbox_SimpleLockpicking_FailChance_too: Chance for the player to fail a lockpick attempt. Not applicable if Can Fail Lockpick is not enabled.
Sandbox_SimpleLockpicking_LosePaperclipO: Determines whether the player breaks a paperclip on a failed lockpick attempt.
Sandbox_SimpleLockpicking_RequireBurglar: Determines whether the player must be a burglar to pick locks.
Sandbox_SimpleSkillBooks_RemoveXPMultipl: If unchecked, the multiplier will be restored. Default is disabled coz it's cheese.
Sandbox_SimpleSuppressors_Debug_tooltip: Enable verbose diagnostics logging. Prints detailed system and feature events to the console.
Sandbox_SimpleSuppressors_DevStartingKit: For testing. New characters start with guns, suppressors, ammo, and the tools needed to craft more.
Sandbox_SimpleSuppressors_FindSuppressor: When off, suppressors and parts never spawn in containers and must be crafted.
Sandbox_SimpleSuppressors_LootRarity_too: Scales relative procedural-loot chances for suppressors and parts. 100 is the baseline; lower or higher values make entries less or more common approximately.
Sandbox_SimpleSuppressors_OilFilterEngin: OIL FILTERS | Missing Oil Filter Engine Damage
Engine condition lost at each missing-oil-filter wear interval.
Sandbox_SimpleSuppressors_OilFilterRemov: OIL FILTERS | Oil Filter Removal Time (seconds)
How long it takes to remove an oil filter from a vehicle engine to salvage it for suppressor crafting.
Sandbox_SimpleSuppressors_OilFilterWearM: OIL FILTERS | Missing Oil Filter Wear Interval
Driving with the oil filter removed damages the engine once per this many in-game minutes. The default is gradual wear: one condition every 10 minutes.
Sandbox_SimpleSuppressors_SoundRadiusRed: How far zombies can hear a suppressed shot, as a percentage of the unsuppressed range. 20 means suppressed shots carry only a fifth as far. 100 disables the effect.
Sandbox_SimpleSuppressors_SoundVolumeRed: How loud a suppressed shot is, as a percentage of the unsuppressed volume. 55 means suppressed shots are slightly more than half as loud. 100 disables the effect.
Sandbox_SitReadFaster_SpeedMultiplier_to: Changes reading speed when reading begins while seated on the ground, furniture, or in a vehicle.\n1.0 = vanilla seated reading speed.\n2.0 = twice that speed.
Sandbox_Skateboard_skateboardImmersive_t: When enabled you will be slower on rough surfaces like gravel/sand.
Sandbox_Skateboard_skateboardRunSpeedMul: Set your player speed when riding the skateboard and holding SHIFT.
Sandbox_Skateboard_skateboardWalkSpeedMu: Set your player speed when riding the skateboard and not holding SHIFT.
Sandbox_SkillCheckType: Select a type of skill check for upgrades
Sandbox_SkillCheckType_tooltip: How should skill levels be applied to upgrades?
Sandbox_SkillJournalAdminOnlyRecover_too: When ON, only admins (or moderators) may press the Recover button. Players can still save snapshots; recovery requires admin sign-off. Useful for hardcore servers that want supervised restoration.
Sandbox_SkillJournalDeathPenalty_tooltip: Levels subtracted from every saved skill on each death before recovery applies. 0 = full restore. 1 or -1 = one-level penalty (default is 1). 5 or -5 = harsh.
Sandbox_SkillJournalFullXpMultipliers: Record active skill-book XP multipliers at full value
Sandbox_SkillJournalFullXpMultipliers_to: Skill books grant a temporary XP multiplier while you are inside their level band. With this on, reading hands those boosts back at the value they had, applied from your current level upward. Off by default: it is a real head start, not just lost progress. While off, skill books are also left out of what a read hands back: a restored page count is enough to collect the whole boost from one more read.
Sandbox_SkillJournalMatchReaderLearningR: Pay out XP at the reader's own learning rate

A skill boost from a profession or trait makes that skill level several times faster, and with no boost at all a skill levels at quarter rate. With this on, XP written down under one character's boosts is converted to what the reader would have had to earn themselves, so a boosted character cannot farm a skill, die, and hand the full total to a character who never paid for the boost. Never pays more than the page holds. Off pays exactly what was written.
Sandbox_SkillJournalMinPlayHours_tooltip: Minimum hours survived on the current character before the first snapshot can be saved. Prevents save-then-suicide exploits on fresh characters. 0 = no gate.
Sandbox_SkillJournalOneReadPerEntry: Each entry can be recovered once per character
Sandbox_SkillJournalOneReadPerEntry_tool: A journal entry pays out once for any given character. Turn this off to let the same entry be read again -- it still only ever hands back the gap between what you have and what was written.
Sandbox_SkillJournalProfessionLock_toolt: When ON, the first Save binds the journal row to your character's profession. Future saves require the same profession, so dying and respawning under a different profession cannot overwrite the snapshot with better stats. Admins can wipe rows from the Blacklist panel. Default ON.
Sandbox_SkillJournalRealHoursCooldown_to: Real-world wall-clock hours that must elapse between two snapshot saves. Independent of in-game time, sleep, or time-skip -- prevents the 'die, respawn fresh, race to re-save better stats' exploit. 0 = disabled. Default 24.
Sandbox_SkillJournalRecoverExerciseRegul: The journal restores how regularly each exercise was being kept up, so a new character does not start their fitness routine from cold. Never lowers what the reader already keeps up. Ignored while physical skills are left out of the journal.
Sandbox_SkillJournalRecoverKills_tooltip: The journal restores the kill count it recorded. Never lowers your current count.
Sandbox_SkillJournalRecoverReading_toolt: The journal restores which books were finished, how far you were through the rest, and the literature, print media and VHS tapes you had already consumed.
Sandbox_SkillJournalRecoverRecipes_toolt: The journal restores recipes you had learned when you wrote in it.
Sandbox_SkillJournalRecoverSkillBookProg: Skill books do two things. They give a temporary XP boost while you are inside the level band the book teaches, and they stay marked as read once you finish them. On, the journal gives both back, so you do not have to find and read those books again, and a boost that was still running returns at the value it had. Off, the journal leaves skill books alone, so a book covering a band you are still inside has to be read again to get its boost back. This setting never affects the XP you recover. Your skills come back at the levels written on the page either way, however fast they were earned.
Sandbox_SkillJournalRecoveryPercentage_t: How much of the gap between your current XP and the XP written in the journal is recovered. 100 restores you fully to what was written. 0 disables skill recovery.
Sandbox_SkillJournalSaveCooldownHours_to: Minimum in-game hours between two consecutive snapshot saves. 0 = unlimited.
Sandbox_SkillJournalSkipPhysical_tooltip: Fitness, Strength and the agility skills (Sprinting, Lightfooted, Nimble, Sneaking) are left out of the journal entirely. Your next character builds their body back themselves; only what they learned carries over.
Sandbox_SkillLegacy_CarryKnowledge: Carry books read and recipes learned
Sandbox_SkillLegacy_CarryKnowledge_toolt: Your next character remembers the skill books you finished and the recipes you learned from magazines. This accumulates across every life: each death adds to what is banked and nothing is ever removed from it. This is never reduced by the death penalty: the percentage is charged against XP, which is progress, whereas re-reading a book you have already read is not a consequence, it is homework. Carried only by a character who inherits -- pick a different profession from last life and you start with nothing read, the same as your skills. Off means every character starts having read nothing, which is vanilla behaviour.
Sandbox_SkillLegacy_Debug_tooltip: Writes a per-skill breakdown to the log on every death and restore: what you started the life with, what you ended with, and exactly what the penalty cost. Use it to confirm the mod is working and to decide whether the percentage feels right.
Sandbox_SkillLegacy_PenaltyPercent_toolt: How much of what you earned in the life that just ended is forfeited. 0 keeps everything, 100 means a life's work dies with you but earlier lives still count. This is a share of your GAINS, not of your total: skills you inherited are never taken away, so dying twice in a row cannot spiral you back to nothing.
Sandbox_SkillLegacy_ReplaceStartingSkill: On a character who has a legacy to inherit, wipe the skill levels granted by their profession and traits, then restore the legacy on top. Your skills then come from what you earned in past lives, not from re-picking a strong profession every time you die. Traits still apply everything else they do. Your FIRST character is never touched -- there is nothing to inherit yet, so their profession works normally.
Sandbox_SkillLegacy_RestoreBuild_tooltip: Adds a CONTINUE LAST SURVIVOR button to the character creation screen, which fills in the profession and traits you died with. You are then free to edit them. 1 = show the button, the default. 2 = fill the build in automatically, with the button still there. 0 = no button and the build is never restored, though skills still carry over. The button is only a convenience: what decides whether you inherit is the PROFESSION you end up with. Pick the one you died as and your skills, books and recipes come with you; pick a different one and you are a new survivor with none of them. Nothing is decided until the character actually spawns, so you can change your mind as often as you like. Your first character sees no button, because there is nothing banked yet.
Sandbox_SkillRecoveryJournalCraftRecipeN: If set to true, crafting the journal requires learning the recipe.\n\nCurrently there is no way to learn it, making the recipe uncraftable.
Sandbox_SkillRecoveryJournalCraftRecipe_:
Leaving this blank will use the default recipe.

Syntax follows vanilla/standard recipe inputs/ingredients.
These are fed directly into a recipe script's input{}. Example:
   item 1 [Base.Notebook;Base.Journal;Base.Diary1;Base.Diary2;Base.Notepad] flags[Prop2] mode:destroy, item 1 tags[base:glue] flags[Prop1], item 3 [Base.LeatherStrips;Base.LeatherStripsDirty] mode:destroy, item 1 tags[base:thread;base:twine;base:heavythread],

Sandbox_SkillRecoveryJournalTranscribeSp: A multiplier on the speed of transcribing journals.
Sandbox_SkillRecoveryJournalTranscribeTV: Toggling this on will allow people to transcribe XP earned from watching TV/VHS. Note: This means players can carry over watched XP between characters cumulatively.
Sandbox_SkillRecoveryJournalUsed_tooltip: Normally you can reread the journal as many times as you like - with this toggled on each individual XP point can only be recovered once. You can still add onto the journal, but each point can only be recovered once on each journal. Note: the tooltip for the journal will now display a fraction for unused points.
Sandbox_SkillRecoveryJournal_SecurityFea: Whether journals check against username, steamID, both, or none. Warning: Disabling this entirely would mean people can share journals.
Sandbox_SkillSpeedBonusPerLevel_tooltip: Search time reduction per Foraging level. Default 0.07 means 7 percent faster per level.
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_AllowClientOverrid: ON: each player can change HUD visibility toggles in Esc > Options > Mods. OFF: everyone uses the sandbox values below (server-wide).
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_Enabled_tooltip: Master switch. OFF replaces the Minecraft-style HUD with the vanilla Project Zomboid hotbar for everyone.
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_HudSize_tooltip: On-screen size of the Minecraft HUD as a percentage. 100 = the original fixed size, 70 = default. Only used when client Mod Options are disabled.
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_ShowArmor_tooltip: Server default / forced value for armor icons.
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_ShowDurability_too: Server default / forced value for item durability bars.
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_ShowHealth_tooltip: Server default / forced value for the heart row.
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_ShowHunger_tooltip: Server default / forced value for hunger icons.
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_ShowStamina_toolti: Server default / forced value for the stamina bar.
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_ShowThirst_tooltip: Server default / forced value for thirst air-bubble icons.
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_ShowXpOrbs_tooltip: Server default / forced value for experience orb VFX when you kill zombies/players/animals.
Sandbox_SkyblockMCHud_XpOrbSounds_toolti: Server default / forced value for absorb sounds when orbs are collected.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ActivityEffectsMultipli: Multiplier for how much physical activities affect fever (0.0 = no effect, 0.5 = half effect, 1.0 = normal, 2.0 = double effect)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_DebugMode_tooltip: Show detailed debug information in console. Only enable for troubleshooting or development.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_DisableOneBlockWake_too: When enabled, zombies won't automatically wake up when you get within 1 tile of them. Your disguise holds even at very close range.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_DisableZombieWalkRunSus: When enabled, running while in Zombie Walk Mode generates zero extra suspicion (instead of a reduced amount). Intended for games using the 'Sprinters' zombie speed setting, where a running shuffle isn't unusual. Off by default.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_FeverDeathDays_tooltip: How many in-game days until terminal fever if you do nothing but rest in ideal conditions (20-365 days)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_FeverEnabled_tooltip: Enables the slow-burning fever mechanic. This replaces the base game fever system for Slow Burn players. When disabled, temperature progression is completely turned off.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_FeverProgressionMultipl: Multiplier for how quickly your fever progresses (0.1 = 10%% speed, 1.0 = normal based on death days, 5.0 = 500%% speed)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_FeverStartingTemp_toolt: Your starting body temperature in Celsius (37.0 = normal human, 37.2 = infected, 40.0 = severe fever)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ForagingRarityMultiplie: Multiplier for medicinal herb spawn rates when foraging (0.1 = very rare, 1.0 = normal, 3.0 = abundant)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_GruntCooldownSeconds_to: How many real-world seconds you must wait between uses of the groan (V key).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_GruntSuspicionReduction: How much suspicion is removed each time you groan like a zombie (V key).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_GutCoveringDurationHour: How many in-game hours the gut covering effect lasts (0.5 = 30 minutes, 2.0 = 2 hours, 24.0 = full day)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_GutCoveringFeverPenalty: Fever progression speed increase when covered in guts (0.0 = no penalty, 0.1 = 10%% faster, 1.0 = 100%% faster)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_GutCoveringSuspicionMul: Suspicion multiplier when covered in zombie guts (0.0 = no suspicion, 0.5 = half suspicion, 1.0 = no benefit)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_HerbEffectivenessMultip: Multiplier for herbal remedy effectiveness (0.1 = 10%% effective, 1.0 = normal, 3.0 = 300%% effective)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ModernMedicineSpawnMult: Multiplier for modern medicine spawn rates in containers (0.0 = never spawns, 1.0 = normal, 3.0 = abundant)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_MovementDetectionRange_: How many tiles away zombies can detect your suspicious movements (5-30 tiles)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_NakedHordeChance_toolti: Percentage chance of a naked horde spawning on each check (0-100%%).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_NakedHordeDespawnDistan: How many tiles away a naked horde's zombies are removed to manage population.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_NakedHordeEnabled_toolt: Periodically spawns a moving cluster of naked zombies passing near you. Unlike ordinary zombies, Naked Horde members do not respect your disguise -- they behave like normal, fully alert zombies and will notice and attack you if you don't stay out of their way.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_NakedHordeIntervalMinut: How often, in REAL-WORLD minutes (not in-game time), the game rolls a chance to spawn a naked horde. Using real time keeps the pacing consistent regardless of your DayLength sandbox setting.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_NakedHordeMaxSize_toolt: Largest number of zombies in a naked horde.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_NakedHordeMinSize_toolt: Smallest number of zombies in a naked horde.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_NakedHordeSpawnAtStart: Spawn Naked Horde at Game Start
Sandbox_SlowBurn_NakedHordeSpawnAtStart_: Forces one naked horde to spawn and pass near your starting location the first time a character spawns.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_NakedHordeSpawnDistance: How many tiles away from you a naked horde spawns.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_NakedZombieChance_toolt: Percentage of ordinary zombies that spawn stripped of their worn clothing (0-100%%). Purely cosmetic -- these zombies still fully respect your disguise, unlike Naked Horde members, which are always naked and always dangerous.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ProximityWakeDistance_t: When you attack a zombie, others within this many tiles will also wake up and attack (0 = only target, 10 = large group response)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ShowFeverTemperature_to: Display your exact fever temperature in moodle tooltips instead of just fever stage.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_SmartZombieChance_toolt: Percentage of 'smart' zombies that can instantly see through your disguise no matter what (0-50%%)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_SuspicionDecayMultiplie: Multiplier for how quickly suspicion decreases when hiding (0.1 = 10%% speed, 1.0 = normal, 5.0 = 500%% speed)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_SuspicionGainMultiplier: Multiplier for how quickly suspicion increases from actions (0.1 = 10%% speed, 1.0 = normal, 5.0 = 500%% speed)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_WeaponSuspicionMultipli: Multiplier for suspicion generated when equipping weapons near zombies (0.0 = no penalty, 1.0 = normal, 3.0 = triple penalty)
Sandbox_SlowBurn_WeatherEffects_tooltip: Weather conditions affect fever progression. Rain and cold slow progression, heat accelerates it.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedBluntHeadSca: How much of a blunt weapon's damage rating converts into bleed damage when a critical hit lands on the head specifically -- a solid crack to the skull can draw blood even without a blade. Always rolls as a Normal wound with no skill scaling. Any other blunt hit (body or a non-critical head hit) never bleeds (0.0 = disabled, 0.02 = default).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedCritMultipli: How much stronger a Graze or Normal bleed is when the hit that caused it was a critical hit (the game's own 'good hit' roll, already unique per weapon). Does not affect Devastating wounds, which are already always fatal (1.0 = no bonus, 2.5 = default).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedDevastatingB: A Devastating wound is always fatal. This is the percentage of the zombie's remaining health removed each second once that happens -- higher kills faster. A hard time limit still forces death a few seconds after a Devastating wound regardless of this setting (0.05 = slowest, 0.35 = default, 1.0 = fastest).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedEnabled_tool: A solid hit from a bladed weapon, piercing tool, or firearm can make a zombie bleed out over time on top of the normal damage it takes -- it keeps fighting while it happens. Every qualifying hit rolls how deep the wound is (see the Devastating/Graze Chance options below).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedGrazeBleedBe: Graze Wound Time Before Clot Check

How many real seconds a Graze wound bleeds unconditionally before it's even eligible for the one-time clot roll below. Prevents a Graze from resolving itself away almost immediately and being pointless (0 = eligible instantly, 10 = default).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedGrazeClotCha: Once a Graze wound has bled for the time above, this is the one-time percentage chance it clots shut and stops for good. If it fails, it keeps bleeding at the low Graze rate until the zombie dies -- no further clot rolls happen for that wound (0%% = every Graze eventually kills, 35%% = default, 100%% = every Graze clots after the time limit).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedGrazeDamageS: How much of a weapon's own damage rating converts into bleed damage per second for a hit that rolled as a Graze. Deliberately weak -- a Graze alone should rarely kill without stacking more hits (0.0 = no bleed, 0.004 = default, 0.5 = maximum).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedHeadDevastat: Percentage chance that a qualifying hit to the head rolls as a Devastating wound. Higher than the torso equivalent by default -- a solid hit to the head is more likely to be lethal (0-100%%, 20%% = default).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedHeadGrazeCha: Percentage chance that a qualifying hit to the head rolls as a minor Graze. Lower than the torso equivalent by default -- a head hit is less likely to be a shrug-off (0-100%%, 40%% = default).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedMaxPerTick_t: Caps how much bleed damage per second a single zombie can accumulate from Graze wounds, and separately from Normal wounds, even from repeated hits, so stacking wounds of the same depth can't produce an absurd instant kill. Does not cap Devastating wounds (2.0 = default).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedNormalBleedB: Normal Wound Time Before Clot Check

How many real seconds a Normal wound bleeds unconditionally before it's even eligible for its own one-time clot roll below. Much longer than the Graze equivalent by default -- a Normal wound is meant to usually kill (0 = eligible instantly, 30 = default).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedNormalClotCh: Once a Normal wound has bled for the time above, this is the one-time percentage chance it clots shut and stops for good. Low by default -- most Normal wounds are still meant to kill, this just allows a rare few to clot given enough time. Devastating wounds never clot regardless of this setting (0%% = every Normal wound eventually kills, 5%% = default).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedNormalDamage: How much of a weapon's own damage rating converts into bleed damage per second for a hit that rolled as a Normal wound -- the 'solid hit' case, usually enough to bleed a zombie out on its own given time (0.0 = no bleed, 0.03 = default, 1.0 = maximum).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedSkillDevasta: Of the percentage shifted out of Graze chance by skill level, the fraction that goes to Devastating chance instead of Normal chance (0.0 = all goes to Normal, 0.4 = default, 1.0 = all goes to Devastating).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedSkillScaling: A more skilled attacker gets better odds of a Normal or Devastating wound instead of a Graze. Only the one real skill governing the weapon actually in hand matters -- a Short Blade 6 / Aiming 1 character gets the Short Blade 6 bonus with a knife, but only the Aiming 1 bonus with a pistol.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedSkillShiftPe: Percentage points moved out of the Graze chance per skill level (0-10) in the relevant weapon skill, split between Normal and Devastating below (0.0 = skill has no effect, 2.5 = default, 10.0 = a single level can shift a third of a typical Graze chance).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedTorsoDevasta: Percentage chance that a qualifying hit to the torso rolls as a Devastating wound -- always fatal, ignores the per-tick cap, can't clot (0-100%%, 5%% = default).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieBleedTorsoGrazeCh: Percentage chance that a qualifying hit to the torso rolls as a minor Graze -- weak bleed that can clot shut on its own. Whatever's left after this and the Devastating chance rolls as a Normal wound (0-100%%, 70%% = default).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieSmashBleedChance_: Percentage chance of cutting yourself on the glass when using Infected Window Break (0-100%%).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieSmashGlovesBleedM: Infected Window Break Gloves Bleed Multiplier
Multiplier applied to the bleed chance when wearing gloves (0.0 = fully protected, 0.1 = massively reduced, 1.0 = no protection).
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieSmashWindowMaxSec: Longest possible time (in real seconds) breaking a window bare-handed like a zombie can take -- randomized each time between the min and this.
Sandbox_SlowBurn_ZombieSmashWindowMinSec: Shortest possible time (in real seconds) breaking a window bare-handed like a zombie can take -- randomized each time between this and the max.

Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BaseEatTime_tool:
This value is used to calculate how long a body takes to be eaten.
It is in real world seconds.
The actual time taken to consume a corpse is adjusted by:
- Size of the body relative(ish) to a human.
- Number of zombies eating the body.
- Current game speed.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyAgeMultiplie: Bodies will have their age (world hours) multiplied by this value, which is then added to the smell distance.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyDispersionAn:
This angle is used to determine whether a zombie falls inside an area that is projected from bodies in the direction of the wind, up to the smell distance.
Set to 0 to disable.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyIndoorCheck_: When enabled (checked), only zombies in the same building as a body are capable of smelling it.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyMaxDistance_: Maximum potential distance of dead body smell
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodySizeImpactsS: When enabled (checked), the size of the body has an effect on the distance.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyStartDistanc: Body smell distance will always start at this value.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyTemperatureP:
This value is divided by the current temperature, to get a multiplier that adjusts the result of [Start Distance + Age Multiplier].
This value is in celsius.
Set to 0 to disable temperature having an effect.
At default, temperatures above 26C increase the distance bodies can be smelled by zombies, while temperatures below 26C decrease the distance.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyWindSpeedMul:
This value is used to determine how much impact the wind speed has on the smell of bodies.
Higher values increase the effect.
Wind has a significant impact on smell distance.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_CanSmellPlayer_t: When enabled (checked), zombies will be able to smell players.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_EatCooldownMulti:
This value controls how often a zombie can eat.

The cooldown increases as they eat, and does not require a body to be fully consumed.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_EatSyncFrequency:
Time in milliseconds between syncing eat progress.
Values greater than 1000 may reduce the accuracy of Base Eat Time.
This is intended for multiplayer usage, to reduce network traffic and log spam caused by RPC.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_FogMultiplier_to:

Sandbox_StarvingZombies_ItemDestroyChanc: When a body is consumed, every individual item has this chance of being destroyed.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_PlayerBloodMulti: The amount of blood on a player, and on items in their inventory, will be multiplied by this value, which is then added to smell distance.

Sandbox_StarvingZombies_PlayerMaxDistanc: Maximum potential distance of player's smell.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_PlayerStartDista: Player smell distance will always start at this value.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_PlayerWindSpeedM:
This value is used to determine how much impact the wind speed has on the smell of the player.
Higher values increase the effect.
Wind has a significant effect on smell distance.

Sandbox_StarvingZombies_RandomSensitivit: When enabled (checked), zombies are assigned a random sensitivity to smell.

Sandbox_TLOU_BloaterArmor_tooltip: Bloater armor hit points, increasing this value will make Bloaters tank longer.
Sandbox_TLOU_BloaterBurnRate_tooltip: Dictates how fast a Bloater will burn and die from fire.
Sandbox_TLOU_BloaterEnergyRequired_toolt: The energy required for a gun caliber to damage a Bloater's armor.
Sandbox_TLOU_BloaterHP_tooltip: 0 means default vanilla zombie health (depends on Bloater toughness).
Sandbox_TLOU_BloaterSpawn_tooltip:
Bloaters are seen as legends by many due to their rarity among infected types. If a Clicker manages to survive over the years, sustaining its body and the Cordycep within, it evolves into a colossus with thick skin protected by Cordyceps patches.
No one wants to contemplate what would happen to a person if they were caught by this creature, so approaching it is out of the question.
Sandbox_TLOU_ClickerArmor_tooltip: Clicker armor hit points, increasing this value will make Clickers tank longer.
Sandbox_TLOU_ClickerBurnRate_tooltip: Dictates how fast a Clicker will burn and die from fire.
Sandbox_TLOU_ClickerEnergyRequired_toolt: The energy required for a gun caliber to damage a Clicker's armor.
Sandbox_TLOU_ClickerHP_tooltip: 0 means default vanilla zombie health (depends on Clicker toughness).
Sandbox_TLOU_ClickerSpawn_tooltip:
Clickers evolve from Stalkers into an even more dangerous state. Their inhuman strength makes them extremely perilous to approach; anyone too close could find themselves dead in mere seconds.
The cries of struggle have long been replaced with a clicking noise, used to replace their lost eyes due to the Cordyceps eating through them.
Fortunately, this alteration makes them slower than simple Runners and Stalkers. However, they will move in unpredictable ways their arms, catching you whenever they get close enough to you.
Sandbox_TLOU_CordycepsSpawnRate_Bloater_: If cordyceps items are allowed to spawn, chose the droprate of it in percentage for Bloaters.
Sandbox_TLOU_CordycepsSpawnRate_Clicker_: If cordyceps items are allowed to spawn, chose the droprate of it in percentage for Clickers.
Sandbox_TLOU_CordycepsSpawnRate_Runner_t: If cordyceps items are allowed to spawn, chose the droprate of it in percentage for Runners.
Sandbox_TLOU_CordycepsSpawnRate_Stalker_: If cordyceps items are allowed to spawn, chose the droprate of it in percentage for Stalkers.
Sandbox_TLOU_CordycepsSpawn_tooltip: Cordyceps items that usually spawn in corpses in the Cordyceps Spore Zones added by Braven will be able to spawn in killed infected. Only works if Cordyceps Spore Zone by Braven is installed.

Minimum infection time from getting infected on the bottom area of the body: upper legs, lower legs, feet.
Sandbox_TLOU_CustomInfectionSystemMiddle: Maximum infection time from getting infected on the middle area of the body: hands, forearms, upper arms, torso, groin.
Minimum infection time from getting infected on the middle area of the body: hands, forearms, upper arms, torso, groin.
Sandbox_TLOU_CustomInfectionSystemTopMax: Maximum infection time from getting infected on the top area of the body: head, neck.
Sandbox_TLOU_CustomInfectionSystemTopMin: Minimum infection time from getting infected on the top area of the body: head, neck.
Sandbox_TLOU_CustomInfectionSystem_toolt: Bites on various area of the body part won't make the player die in the same time. The higher on the body the bites are, the faster your character gets zombified. The transmission settings still apply but the infection mortality is replaced.
Sandbox_TLOU_ExtraFireDamage_Bloater_too:
Bloaters will have their armor weakened when set on fire and will take more damage.
A value of 0 deactivates the extra damage, a value of 1 means 100%% extra damage, a value of 2 means 200%% extra damage...
Sandbox_TLOU_ExtraFireDamage_Clicker_too:
Clickers will have their armor weakened when set on fire and will take more damage.
A value of 0 deactivates the extra damage, a value of 1 means 100%% extra damage, a value of 2 means 200%% extra damage...

Sandbox_TLOU_FEDRASOLDIERSPAWN: Spawn Chance of FEDRA Soldier Zombie of 1000000
Sandbox_TLOU_GrabbyBloaters_tooltip: Bloaters can grab you, making you unable to move.
Sandbox_TLOU_GrabbyClickers_tooltip: Clickers can grab you, making you unable to move. You can save yourself with short blades if you time it well. By default is deactivated due to how unfair it can be but if you want an even harder challenge, go for it.
Sandbox_TLOU_HideIndoorsUpdates_tooltip: Defines how often Infected will check buildings to move towards or roam outside at night. This number shouldn't be kept too low but if you set it too high the Infected might not have time to go in buildings or roam outside at night. On the other hand, you can set it to higher values so they have time to roam around the map. (such as map sounds like alarms or gun shots)
Sandbox_TLOU_HideIndoors_tooltip: All the infected besides Runners have a tendency to hide from the sun within the dark corners of buildings. This makes exploration of a building particularly dangerous while the streets are safer. Make sure to pay attention to your surrondings when exploring.
Sandbox_TLOU_MaxDistanceToCheck_tooltip: Defines the max distance an Infected will check for buildings. The higher the value, the harder the performance impact might be (unsure how hard it hits performances).
Sandbox_TLOU_NoPushBloaters_tooltip: Makes players unable to push Bloaters.
Sandbox_TLOU_NoPushClickers_tooltip: Makes players unable to push Clickers.
Sandbox_TLOU_NoStompClickers_tooltip: Makes players unable to head stomp Clickers with their foot. This means Clickers won't take any damage from stomping with your feet.
Sandbox_TLOU_OneShotClickers_tooltip: Clickers will one shot you, this trait is definitely the most punishing one.
Sandbox_TLOU_OnlyUnexplored_tooltip: Infected will go hide only in unexplored areas. If unchecked then expect some guests in your house. If you've explored every buildings in an area, this could also mean you would find all the Infected types in the street which isn't ideal, especially with respawn on.
Sandbox_TLOU_RunnerBurnRate_tooltip: Dictates how fast a Runner will burn and die from fire.

Sandbox_TLOU_RunnerSpawn_tooltip:
Runners are dangerous and fast humans recently infected by the Cordyceps fungus. They can quickly overwhelm you with their sheer speed and numbers.
You may hear them talking and struggling from within, with the soul of the host likely still present but unable to control their body.

Clickers and Bloaters use an armor system and react accordingly to the energy of the caliber of the gun used. Heavy melee weapons will break this armor easier but normal melee weapons are incapable of breaking through. When the armor breaks, the infected takes extra damage.
Each calibers have a minimum energy and a maxium energy. A caliber needs to have a higher minimum energy value than the required energy to break an infected armor. If only the maximum value is above the needed energy, a coin flip determines if the shot will damage the armor. Based on how high the energy of the caliber is, it will break through the armor better.

Sandbox_TheDarknessIsComing2_stressHealt: Damages player health when stress is high during darkness. Damage scales with stress level.

Sandbox_TheDarknessIsComing2_weatherEnab: If enabled, it will add snowfall and lower the temperature, if temperature is higher than this value. Just like Silent Hill's fog world.
Sandbox_TheDarknessIsComing2_zombieMutat: Zombies change speed based on percentage during darkness events.
