Sandbox_WanderingZombies_TryStopVirtual_: Monitor zed pathing to try and stop them walking outside the active area around a player
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_UpdateMsLimit_t:
Maximum amount of milliseconds that the update can run for
Update runs once per frame
16.67ms is the time limit per frame for a stable 60fps
With a low zombie limit, it should not be necessary to change this value
Horde updates have a hardcoded cap of 2ms that is separate from this value
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_UpdateZedLimit_:
Maximum amount of zeds that can be processed per update
Update runs once per frame
At 60fps, a zed limit of 20 would mean 1200 zeds per second are processed
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_WanderChanceDro:
The chance that zombies will move randomly.

Static: The value chosen below is the value that is always used.
Random: A random value from Min to Max (inclusive) is chosen at random.
The value is randomised when the current period of activity has elapsed (Start Hour to [Start Hour + Total Hours].
If Min is greater than Max, Max will be used as the minimum.
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_WanderChanceMin:
Chance that zombies will move randomly.

/FF0000Increase this value to increase difficulty/FFFFFF.
/00FF00Decrease this value to decrease difficulty/FFFFFF.
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_WanderCooldownH:
The amount of time that must elapse before the next period of activity.
If this value is not a multiple of 24, Start Hour will be modified by the remaining hours.
For example, if Start Hour is set to 0 (midnight), and Cooldown Hours is set to 26, the next Start Hour would be 2am.

Static: The value chosen is the value that is always used.
Random: A random value from Min to Max (inclusive) is chosen at random.
The value is randomised when the current period of activity has elasped (Start Hour to [Start Hour + Total Hours]).
If Min is greater than Max, Max is used as the minimum.
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_WanderDestructi:
Always: Zombies will always attack objects in their path.
Indoors: Only zombies considered indoors will attack objects in their path.
Never: Zombies will not attack objects in their path.
Random: When the period of activity elapses, one of the above three options will be chosen at random.

The vanilla destruction settings do NOT have an effect on this setting.
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_WanderStartHour:
The hour at which random wandering can start.

Static: The value chosen below is the value that is always used.
Random: A random value from Min to Max (inclusive) is chosen at random.
The value is randomised when the current period of activity has elapsed (Start Hour to [Start Hour + Total Hours].
Min is allowed to be greater than Max, so ranges over midnight can be used.

The hour at which random wandering can start.
0 is midnight (12:00am).
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_WanderTotalHour:
This is added to Start Hour to determine the period of activity.

Static: The value chosen is the value that is always used.
Random: A random value from Min to Max (inclusive) is chosen at random.
The value is randomised when the current period of activity has elapsed (Start Hour to [Start Hour + Total Hours]).
If Min is greater than Max, Max will be used as the minimum.
Sandbox_WarHammer_SpawnRate_tooltip: Sets the extra spawn rate of War Hammers
Sandbox_WashAllSecondsPerItem_tooltip: Animation time scales linearly with dirty item count using this many seconds per item.
Sandbox_WashAllWaterPerItem_tooltip: Water cost (in litres) consumed per dirty item the action processes.
Sandbox_WashOrRot_BloodinessIncreaseDecr: A multiplier that will increase or decrease the rate for the time until effects. By default it will take around 3 days of being with over 50%% of body bloodiness to reach to Grimed Moodle Lv1 (Only works if bloodiness mechanic is enabled).
Sandbox_WashOrRot_ClothingBloodinessPerc: Bloodiness percentage that will be transfered to be player's body from each piece of clothing (Only works if bloodiness mechanic is enabled).
Sandbox_WashOrRot_ClothingDirtinessPerce: Dirtiness percentage that will be transfered to be player's body from each piece of clothing (Only works if dirtiness mechanic is enabled).
Sandbox_WashOrRot_DirtinessIncreaseDecre: A multiplier that will increase or decrease the rate for the time until effects. By default it will take around 3 days of being with over 50%% of body dirtiness to reach to Grimed Moodle Lv1 (Only works if dirtiness mechanic is enabled).
Sandbox_WashOrRot_EnableItchingMechanic_: When the grimed Moodle is present, the player will feel itching all over the body, playing a scratch animation and increasing pain to the corresponding body part (It requires either dirtiness mechanic, bloodines mechanic or both mechanics enabled).
Sandbox_WashOrRot_EnableSicknessMechanic: When the grimed Moodle is present at Lv3 or Lv4, there are chances of getting sick, at fever level the body health will decrease which can lead to death (It requires either dirtiness mechanic, bloodines mechanic or both mechanics enabled).
Sandbox_WashOrRot_MinimumClothingBloodin: The minimum amount of bloodiness that each piece of clothing needs to have in order to transfer some of it to the player's body (Only works if bloodiness mechanic is enabled).
Sandbox_WashOrRot_MinimumClothingDirtine: The minimum amount of dirtiness that each piece of clothing needs to have in order to transfer some of it to the player's body (Only works if dirtiness mechanic is enabled).
Sandbox_WashSmart_AllowTaintedWater: Allow Tainted Water to Clean Rags
Sandbox_WashSmart_AllowTaintedWater_tool: When enabled, tainted water can be used to clean rags, bandages and strips.
Sandbox_WashSmart_BandageWaterPerItem_to: Water units used per item when washing dirty bandages, rags, denim strips, and leather strips at a water source. Default: 4.0.
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_ExpirationMax: Maximum Days Until Water Goes Bad
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_ExpirationMax_toolt: In days, the latest the water can go bad. This only starts counting after the water shutoff.
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_ExpirationMin: Minimum Days Until Water Goes Bad
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_ExpirationMin_toolt: In days, the earliest the water can go bad. This only starts counting after the water shutoff.
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_MinimumWaterLeft_to: Amount of water that will not be drained from taps by as a fraction of their total capacity. For example, if this value is 0.2, a tap will not drain past 20%% of its total capacity.
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_NeedFilterWater_too: Players must add filters to their plumbed sinks to clean the water. Otherwise, plumbed sinks are always safe water, even if their water source isn't (like vanilla).
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_ReduceWaterOverTime: After the water shutoff, water will drain from the taps.
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_ScaleWaterLoss_tool: Larger water containers such as baths will lose water faster than sinks.
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_TapSizeScalar_toolt: Multiplier to the water capacity of taps. Does not affect other liquid containers. <LINE> Changing this mid-save does not change the capacity of already loaded taps.
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_WaterReductionChanc: Chance, per day, for water to be removed, to add variance.
Sandbox_WaterGoesBad_WaterReductionRate_: How much water will be removed from each tap per day as a fraction of their total capacity. For example, if this value is 0.2, a tap will lose 20%% of its maximum water each day. Individual taps will have slight random variance from this value. <LINE> If set to 1, all taps will reach their minimum value immediately when the water shuts off. <LINE> If set to 0, water will not drain.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_DripBurstPressure: Pressure that bursts a drip emitter (tenths)
Sandbox_WaterPipes_DripBurstPressure_too: Above this pressure a drip emitter blows out and stops watering until you repair it, just like a real one. In tenths of a metre of water column: 150 = 15.0, well under a pump's 25.0, so a pump on the same line will burst your emitters unless you put a router in between and set a limit. Set to 0 so emitters never burst.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_GeneratorRefuelTarget: When auto-refuelling, the generator is topped up to this percentage of its tank (100 = full).
Sandbox_WaterPipes_GeneratorRefuelThresh: A plumbed generator pulls fuel from the network once its tank drops below this percentage of its capacity. Set to 0 to disable auto-refuelling.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_HydrantHead_tooltip: Pressure an open, mains-fed fire hydrant holds its network at, in tenths of a metre of water column. 400 = 40.0, well above the household mains (25.0) and a sprinkler's 20.0, because a hydrant is a high-flow tap on the town main. Opening one runs sprinklers far from any barrel with no pump, right up to the day the water is cut, after which the hydrant still yields its reserve but with no pressure. Lower it to make hydrants less of a free pump.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_HydrantReserve_toolti: How much water a fire hydrant still holds in its local main once the town water is cut. 1000 by default. While the water service is on the hydrant is mains-fed and effectively bottomless; this is only what is left afterwards, and it drains as you use it. Set to 0 so hydrants run dry the moment the water stops.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_MainsHead_tooltip: Pressure the town supply holds the network at, in tenths of a metre of water column. 250 = 25.0, the low end of what a real municipal main runs. A sprinkler needs 20.0, so at the default the mains runs sprinklers on its own. Lower it if you want pumps to still matter before the shutoff.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_MainsIntakeRate: Town water intake rate (litres per minute)
Sandbox_WaterPipes_MainsIntakeRate_toolt: How much water the town supply pushes into your network each in-game minute. 60 = 3600 litres an hour, three times a pump, because the mains is the fattest source in the game. Lower it if filling your whole reserve before the shutoff feels too easy.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_MainsSupply_tooltip: While the water service is still running, a plumbed sink or shower feeds your pipes instead of just drawing from them: it fills your containers and holds the network at mains pressure, so sprinklers run without a pump until the day the water is cut. Turn this off to keep the old behaviour, where plumbing a fixture switched its town water off and gave nothing back.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PressureContainerBase: Pressure a barrel or collector provides on its own floor, in tenths of a metre of water column, from the weight of its own water. 10 = 1.0, which lets a tap draw from about 20 tiles away on the flat. Raise this if taps in your base sit a long way from their barrels.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PressureFrictionScale: How much pressure each pipe tile costs, as a percentage of the default. 100 = default. 200 = pipes lose pressure twice as fast, halving how far water travels. Set to 0 so distance never costs pressure and only height and pumps matter.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PressureModel_tooltip: How water pressure is worked out. Pressure is measured in metres of water column: height above a tap adds pressure, distance along the pipes spends it, and pumps create it. Realistic uses the full model. Simple counts height only, so distance never costs anything. Off restores the old behaviour, where water simply flows downhill however far it has to travel.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PressurePerLevel: Pressure gained per floor of height (tenths)
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PressurePerLevel_tool: Pressure a source gains for each floor it sits above what it feeds, in tenths of a metre of water column. 30 = 3.0 per floor, which matches a real storey height. Higher values make rooftop tanks and water towers stronger.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PumpFromWaterBodies: Pumps can draw from rivers and lakes
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PumpFromWaterBodies_t: When on, a pump placed beside open water draws unlimited dirty water from it, which you can then clean with a purifier. Turn this off to keep water scarce: pumps will still work from wells and from your own barrels.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PumpHead_tooltip: Pressure a powered pump adds to its part of the network, in tenths of a metre of water column. 250 = 25.0, which matches a domestic pressure set. Pumps chained together add up. A sprinkler needs 20.0, so one pump runs sprinklers about 30 tiles away.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PumpIntakeRate_toolti: How much water a pump draws from a well or open water each in-game minute. 20 = about 1200 litres an hour, which is on the modest side for a real pump. This is the main brake on infinite river water, so lower it if water feels too easy.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PumpSuctionLimit_tool: How far below itself a pump can still lift water, in tenths of a metre of water column. 70 = 7.0, about two floors, which is the real limit for a surface pump because atmospheric pressure caps suction. A source further down will not prime, no matter how strong the pump is. Raise this if you want pumps to reach deep basements.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_PurifierFilterWear_to: How fast the electric purifier's filter wears out with use, as a percentage of the default rate. 100 = default (a full filter cleans about 5000 units of tainted water before it needs repair). 200 = wears twice as fast, 50 = half as fast. Set to 0 so filters never wear out and never need repairing.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_RainTaintsOpenWater_t: When on, rain falling on an open container left outside taints its whole network, so uncovered collection is a gamble whenever the weather turns. Turn off if you would rather open containers only spoil from sitting still.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_RealisticPurification: When on, taps no longer purify tainted water automatically: tainted water stays tainted until you run it through a purifier tile. On by default as the survival baseline; turn it off to have taps serve clean water like vanilla.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_SmartPipes: Enable pre-fill and optimal water levels (aka Smart pipes).
Sandbox_WaterPipes_SmartPipesFillMax: SmartPipes: Maximum amount of water added per watering cycle.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_SmartPipesUpdateNotWa: SmartPipes: Update "last watered" counter even when no water was used.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_SprinklerNoise_toolti: When on, a running sprinkler attracts zombies, which is the price you pay for watering a whole area at once. Turn it off if you would rather irrigate quietly.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_StagnationDaysClosed: Days before sealed water goes bad
Sandbox_WaterPipes_StagnationDaysClosed_: How many days a sealed container (a covered tank, the pipe network itself, a lidded amphora) may sit with no movement before its water turns tainted. Sealed water keeps for weeks, so this is the long timer. Set to 0 so sealed water never goes bad.
Sandbox_WaterPipes_StagnationDaysOpen: Days before open water goes bad
Sandbox_WaterPipes_StagnationDaysOpen_to: How many days an open, rain-catching container (a rain barrel, an uncovered amphora) may sit with no movement before its water turns tainted. Open water spoils in days, so this is the short timer. Set to 0 so open water never goes bad on its own (rain can still taint it).
Sandbox_WaterPipes_WaterStagnation_toolt: When on, water left sitting in a container or pipe network turns tainted after a while, and rain contaminates any open water left outside. Drawing from a network, refilling it, or town water flowing through it all count as movement and keep it fresh. Turn off to keep stored water clean forever.
Sandbox_WayMoreCars: More Car Features + Spawn Zones Expansion
Sandbox_WeddingRingEffects_tooltip: Subtle effects when both partners are wearing wedding rings.
Sandbox_WeightReduction_AffectTools_tool: Also reduce the weight of tools such as hammers, saws, axes, crowbars and sledgehammers. Turn off to keep tools at their normal weight while still lightening materials.
Sandbox_WeightReduction_ReductionPercent: How much weight is removed from building materials, tools and paint. 95 means an item weighs 5%% of its normal weight. Set to 0 to disable.
Sandbox_WeightThreshhold95_EnableTraitTh: When enabled, Overweight appears only after reaching the selected threshold. When disabled, the vanilla 85 kg threshold is used.
Sandbox_WeightThreshhold95_WeightGainMul: 1.0 keeps the vanilla speed; 0.5 halves weight gain speed.
Sandbox_WeightThreshhold95_WeightLossMul: 1.0 keeps the vanilla speed; 0.5 halves weight loss speed.
Sandbox_WeightThreshhold95_Weight_toolti: The weight at which the character gains Overweight. Default: 95 kg.
Sandbox_WeightThreshold95_EnableTraitThr: When enabled, Overweight appears only after reaching the selected threshold. When disabled, the vanilla 85 kg threshold is used.
Sandbox_WeightThreshold95_WeightGainMult: 1.0 keeps the vanilla speed; 0.5 halves weight gain speed.
Sandbox_WeightThreshold95_WeightLossMult: 1.0 keeps the vanilla speed; 0.5 halves weight loss speed.
Sandbox_WeightThreshold95_Weight_tooltip: The weight at which the character gains Overweight. Default: 95 kg.
Sandbox_WellDeadBodiesRadius_tooltip: The radius (in tiles) around a well within which dead bodies can contaminate the water.
Sandbox_WellMinBetweenDistanceToFullRefi: Min Distance Between Wells to Refill
Minimum distance (in tiles) required between wells in order for them to fully refill. Prevents clustering multiple wells too close together for resource gain.
Sandbox_WellWaterPerCycleMultiplier_tool: Multiplier applied to the water refill rate of the well. Higher values increase the total water generated per cycle.
Sandbox_WellWaterRainFactor_tooltip: Additional multiplier applied to the water refill rate of the well when it is raining. This simulates the effect of rainwater contributing to the well's water supply.
Sandbox_WhereIWas: Where I Was When It Happened
Sandbox_WhereIWas.ActiveScenario_tooltip: Single-player only. The selected scenario is applied when creating a new world; existing worlds are not converted. No Scenario keeps the ordinary Project Zomboid start.
Sandbox_WhereIWas.OptionalChallenge_tool: Show and track the selected scenario's optional objective. Leave disabled for a themed starting situation without challenge notifications or completion tracking.
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_AllowGroundKeys: Allow naming keys on the ground
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_AllowGroundKeys_t: On by default. Shows the name of a key lying on the ground nearby, above the key itself. When off, it is not shown even if a player has it enabled in their own mod options.
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_MovedBodyCountsAs: Hauling the body off counts as taking it

On by default. Multiplayer only, and only when "Stop following once another survivor takes it" above is on. Following stops once somebody moves the body well away from where it fell - dragged, loaded into a vehicle or stored in a container - even though the ring was never taken out of it. Off, and the mark follows the body wherever it goes. Shifting it out of a doorway is not enough to stop anything.
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_RequireCompass_to: Off by default, since it is a lot to ask in singleplayer. When on, distances, the map jump and the direction pointer only work while you carry a compass. Independent of the other rules. Renaming keys always works.
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_RequireExplored: Require the area to be uncovered on the map
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_RequireExplored_t: On by default. A key only shows its location if that part of the world map has already been uncovered - by walking there, or by a map you have read. Keys pointing into the blank stay hidden until you find the place. Independent of the other rules.
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_RequireMapItem: Require a map of the area
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_RequireMapItem_to: Off by default. When on, a key's location is only readable if you carry a paper map covering that spot - but once you have read a key's location it stays readable, map or not. Independent of the other rules.
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_StopWhenTaken: Stop following once another survivor takes it
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_StopWhenTaken_too: On by default. Multiplayer only. Following stops the moment another survivor takes the key ring out of your body and into their own pockets. Off, and the mark follows them instead. Dragging your body about or loading it into a car is not taking your ring, so the mark stays either way.
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_TakerCanStop: Whoever picks it up may switch the follow off
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_TakerCanStop_tool: On by default. Multiplayer only. Someone who picks up a ring carrying another survivor's mark gets a right-click option to switch that mark off, which stops the follow on the other end too. Off, and the mark is not theirs to touch.
Sandbox_WhoseKeyIsThis_TrackLostKeyRings: Allow following a key ring after death  -  adds a key ring tab to the map

On by default. When a key ring marked to be followed leaves a player's inventory - most often on the body they left behind - the last place it was seen is marked until it is picked up again. It is also what puts the key ring tab in the map's key list. When off, no player follows rings and no tab appears, however they have their own mod options set.

Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_AntibioticCourse_:
How much cover it takes to beat an infection. 1.0 is 48 hours - three antibiotics back to back, the balance the mod was built around.
Lower it on a world where medicine is scarce: 0.66 makes it a two-pill course, 0.33 a single one. Higher makes a cure a project.
It does not change how fast the illness climbs - that is the sepsis speed setting.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_BloodLossEnabled_: Heavy bleeding leaves the survivor weak for days after the cut is dressed.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_BloodWarmHours_to:
How many in-game hours drawn blood stays usable while warm. Real blood banks allow 4; the default is 8 so a trip home is possible.
A powered fridge stops the clock, a cooler slows it six times, winter air at 6 C or below keeps blood that is not being carried on a body.
A freezer ruins whole blood.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_CoveredWoundsHidd:
A bandaged limb shows only the bandage, a broken bone, and whether it hurts. The kind of wound, stitches and infection stay hidden until the dressing comes off.
What was examined before is remembered: removing the bandage shows it without a new examination.
Off: wounds read through the bandage as before.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_ExamineScalesWith:
On: a limb with little on it is a glance and a limb with a lot on it is a real examination - one scratch takes about half the base time, three findings take all of it.
Off (the default): every examination takes the flat time set by skill and the speed slider, however much or little there is to find.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_ExamineSpeed_tool:
How quickly an examination is carried out. Higher is faster.
First Aid still shortens it on top of this.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_FractureEnabled_t:
A broken bone under an open wound worsens while unsplinted and feeds the infection.
Arms and legs only.
Also needs the Bone Fracture option enabled, or nothing can break in the first place.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_GateMiniHealthPan: Quick health panels wait for the examination

Only matters with Mini Health Panel or Mini Health Plus installed. Their floating window offers treatment without an examination, which walks around this mod's central rule.
On: their menu is held on an unexamined limb, same as this mod's own panel.
Off: their panel stays a fast lane - on some servers a neck wound is a matter of seconds, and one screen too many before a bandage can be a death.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_MedicalItemsEnabl:
Turns on the blood part of the mod: drawing blood, transfusion, blood groups, typing and crossmatching - and puts the supplies for it in hospital and clinic loot: blood collection bags (single-use, the only vessel blood goes into), a transfusion set and a blood typing kit.
OFF by default. While off, none of it is offered and none of the items ever spawn - the mod stays pure Lua and can be removed at any time.
Turning it on lets mod items into your save.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_NeckSkipsExaminat:
A cut throat empties a survivor in well under a minute, and an untrained character spends twelve seconds looking before they are allowed to touch it.
On: the neck can be treated on sight, like vanilla.
Off: it waits for an examination like every other limb.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_PoisoningEnabled_:
Taking more medicine than the body can clear makes you ill for far longer than the overdose itself lasts, and leaves a mark on the liver and kidneys.
Alcohol on top of a course of medicine is much harder on the liver than alcohol alone.
Water helps: a hydrated survivor clears an overdose about twice as fast, and healthy kidneys are what makes that work.
Turned off, medicine behaves as it did before this was added - an overdose still makes you sick while it lasts, but nothing accumulates.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_RequireExaminatio:
The body always shows where it hurts and how badly. This decides how much of the naming an examination has to do first - and First Aid decides how fast and how detailed that examination is.
Everything: nothing is named until you look, treatment included.
Only what you cannot feel: an injury you watched happen is named at once, and looking is for infection, dirt and how far it has got.
Nothing: everything is named straight away, the way vanilla does it.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_SepsisEnabled_too:
An untreated wound infection reaches the bloodstream and kills.
Antibiotics work as a course over days, not as a single pill.
Turned off, wound infection behaves as it does in vanilla.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_SepsisSpeed_toolt:
How fast an infection takes hold and climbs. 1.0 is the balance the mod was built around: untreated, the first symptoms arrive after about twelve hours and it kills in roughly three days.
Lower is milder. It never makes the body recover faster, only the illness slower.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_SutureGameEnabled:
On: stitching opens a close-up of the wound and you place each stitch yourself - the needle goes in one side and out the other, and how well it is done is up to you. First Aid decides how steady your hand is; a surgical needle forgives more than a sewing one. A poor closure can tear open when you run.
Off: stitching works exactly as it does in vanilla, decided by a dice roll behind the scenes.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_TreatmentNeedsExa:
On the strictest examination setting, a limb cannot be treated until it has been examined - you cannot bandage what you have not looked at.
Turn this off to keep the naming behind an examination while letting first aid go ahead: you can dress a wound in a hurry and find out what it is later, somewhere safer.
Has no effect on the other two examination settings, where nothing was held back to begin with.
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_WalkingExamSkill: First Aid needed to examine while walking:
Sandbox_WoundsOverhaul_WalkingExamSkill_:
Below this First Aid level an examination roots the character in place. 0 allows walking from the start, 10 never.
Legs, feet and groin always require standing still - that is anatomy, not skill.

Sandbox_ZTA_AggroRadius_tooltip:
How close a zombie must be to an animal before it starts 
hunting it. Measured animal-to-zombie, not from you. 
Once hunting, it keeps chasing until twice this distance, 
so a fleeing animal cannot shake it by a few tiles.
Sandbox_ZTA_BiteDamage_tooltip: Damage per bite. Higher means animals go down faster.
Sandbox_ZTA_CompanionDogTargeting_toolti: Controls if your pet can be attacked by zombies.
Sandbox_ZTA_CompanionDogToughness_toolti:
How tough your dog is: 
(Average) - Lassie: a regular dog, about 10 bites 
(Tough) - Max: battle hardened, about 20 bites 
(Rambo) - Krypto: super hero canine, about 50 bites
Sandbox_ZTA_Enabled_tooltip: Zombies will chase and kill nearby animals instead of ignoring them.
Sandbox_ZTA_Feast_tooltip: After a kill, nearby zombies gather and feed on the carcass. \nHow many can feed at once scales with the animal's size, \nup to four on a full-grown cow.
Sandbox_ZTA_FightBack_tooltip:
Bulls, rams, boars and roosters charge and gore zombies once 
wounded. They flee at half health, then fight to the death. 
An enraged animal is dangerous to you as well. 
Stallions from the Horse Mod charge too, trampling rather 
than goring - but only if horses are targets at all.
Sandbox_ZTA_GoreDamage_tooltip: Damage an enraged animal does to a zombie per hit. At the \ndefault it takes roughly three or four hits to put one down. \nWhat it does to YOU is set separately, just below.
Sandbox_ZTA_HerdDefense_tooltip:
When a female or young animal is attacked, the nearest male 
of its species enrages and charges her attackers: bulls answer 
for cows and calves, rams for ewes and lambs, boars, roosters 
and stallions likewise.
Sandbox_ZTA_HorseTargeting: Horse Mod horses as zombie targets
Sandbox_ZTA_HorseTargeting_tooltip:
Only applies if the Horse Mod is installed. 
Horses count as livestock, so this also needs "Include 
livestock" turned on before it changes anything. 
"Only when not ridden" leaves a loose horse at risk out in 
a field, but zombies never go for the horse you are riding.
Sandbox_ZTA_IncludeLivestock_tooltip:
Farm animals, and horses from the Horse Mod. 
Turn this off and zombies hunt only wildlife, leaving your 
own herds alone. 
Turning BOTH this and "Include wild animals" off means 
nothing is hunted at all, which is the same as switching 
the mod off.
Sandbox_ZTA_IncludeWild_tooltip:
Deer, rabbits, raccoons and rodents are hunted too. 
Turn this off to restrict hunting to livestock. Stray and 
wild dogs have their own share slider in the Companion 
Dogs section below (20%% by default).
Sandbox_ZTA_KnockdownChance_tooltip:
Chance that a gore also knocks the zombie to the ground. 
BULLS IGNORE THIS and always knock down -- a ton of charging 
animal is not a dice roll. This chance governs the lighter 
fighters: rams, boars, roosters, and stallion tramples.
Sandbox_ZTA_MaxPerAnimal_tooltip:
How many zombies can hunt the same animal at once; extra 
zombies ignore it (they do not queue). Zombies already 
hunting are never kicked off by the limit. Keeps huge 
pile-ons down, which also helps performance in horde 
scenes. 0 = unlimited, the behavior of older versions.
Sandbox_ZTA_MotherDefense_tooltip:
A mother stays near her young, escorts it when zombies give 
chase, and rams the one zombie that closes on it - weaker than 
the males, no crowd knockdowns. If the young dies, she flees, 
broken, and will not defend again for a long while.
Sandbox_ZTA_PlayerGorePercent_tooltip:
How hard an enraged animal hits YOU, as a percentage of 
what it does to a zombie. A player is rarely at full health, 
and at 100 an unlucky goring could finish off a wounded one. 
Set to 0 to make enraged animals harmless to players.
Sandbox_ZTA_ProcessRadius_tooltip:
Performance guard for large herds. Animals farther than this 
from every player are ignored by the hunt entirely until 
approached -- no distance checks, no engagement, no cost. 
Never set below twice the aggro radius; the mod enforces 
that floor automatically so ongoing chases are never cut.
Sandbox_ZTA_RagdollFalls_tooltip:
Gored zombies fall as physics ragdolls instead of playing 
the standard knockdown animation. Singleplayer only, and 
needs "physics hit reactions" enabled in the game's display 
options. Turn off if you prefer the classic knockdown or 
notice a performance cost in large fights.
Sandbox_ZTA_RotHours_tooltip: How old a zombie-killed carcass is treated as being. \nHigher is more thoroughly spoiled. An old carcass also \nyields less meat, which hardly matters when it is rotten.
Sandbox_ZTA_RottenMeat_tooltip: Meat butchered from an animal killed by zombies is rotten.
Sandbox_ZTA_SatiationHours_tooltip: How long after a feast zombies remain full and will not \nactively hunt or engage the player unless close. \nIn-game hours; 0 turns this off.
Sandbox_ZTA_ShoutBreakRadius_tooltip: How far the shout reaches hunting zombies. Kept tighter \nthan the shout's full sound radius on purpose, so distant \npacks stay on their prey and only the nearby danger turns.
Sandbox_ZTA_ShoutBreak_tooltip: Determines if shouting pulls aggro from hunting zombies \nto yourself.
Sandbox_ZTA_SpeedNearLivestock_tooltip:
Determines if zombies increase speed to hunt animals (not 
players). 
One tier faster (default): while hunting, zombies upgrade: 
Slow Shambler -> Fast Shambler 
Fast Shambler -> Sprinter 
All become sprinters: 
Slow and Fast Shamblers become sprinters for the hunt. 
MULTIPLAYER SERVERS: consider Off. The boost is this mod's 
largest per-frame cost, and penned farm animals cannot 
outrun zombies anyway.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetCats: Cats Mod cats as zombie targets
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetCats_tooltip:
Only applies if the Cats Mod is installed. Off by default: 
cats are slow and deliberately never flee zombies (a Cats 
Mod pathing fix), so hunted cats die almost instantly. Turn 
on only if you want strays and pets at real risk. Not 
affected by the wild/livestock master switches.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetCattle_tooltip: Cows, bulls and calves. Only applies while the matching \nmaster switch above (livestock) is on.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetChickens_tooltip: Hens, roosters and chicks. Only applies while the matching \nmaster switch above (livestock) is on.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetDeer_tooltip: Bucks, does and fawns. Only applies while the matching \nmaster switch above (wild animals) is on.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetMice_tooltip: Only applies while the matching master switch above \n(wild animals) is on.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetPigs_tooltip: Sows, boars and piglets. Only applies while the matching \nmaster switch above (livestock) is on.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetRabbits_tooltip: Only applies while the matching master switch above \n(wild animals) is on.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetRaccoons_tooltip: Only applies while the matching master switch above \n(wild animals) is on.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetRats_tooltip: Only applies while the matching master switch above \n(wild animals) is on.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetSheep_tooltip: Ewes, rams and lambs. Only applies while the matching \nmaster switch above (livestock) is on.
Sandbox_ZTA_TargetTurkeys_tooltip: Turkey hens, gobblers and poults. Only applies while the \nmatching master switch above (livestock) is on.
Sandbox_ZTA_WildDogHuntPercent_tooltip: %% of spawned wild dogs hunted by zombies - (0-100%%). \nHigher numbers have a greater impact on mod performance, \nparticularly in cities.
Sandbox_ZTA_WoundSlow_tooltip: An injured animal loses speed, so a chase can actually end. \nWith this off, a healthy animal in the open usually escapes.
Sandbox_ZT_Aggression_tooltip: Multiplier on horde sizes the brain is allowed to request.
Sandbox_ZT_AllowAtmospheric_tooltip: When off, the Director skips non-spawn flavor: ambient sounds, phantom gunshots, radio static, and meta-event nudges (helicopter/distant gunfire).
Sandbox_ZT_AllowCulling_tooltip: Lets the tactician remove far-off, off-screen, non-combatant zombies to free up spawn capacity. Never affects zombies near the player or in line of sight.
Sandbox_ZT_AllowLures_tooltip: When off, the Director will not lure existing zombies or redirect them toward players (lure_existing / redirect_zombies). No new zombies are involved either way.
Sandbox_ZT_AllowRuntimeSpawns_tooltip: When off, the Director never spawns hordes or runs sieges (spawn_horde / siege_phase). Use this on dedicated servers if runtime-spawned zombies cause sync glitches. Taunts, lures, atmospherics and weather still work.
Sandbox_ZT_AllowWeatherControl_tooltip: Lets the cognitive brain trigger weather events. Manual Control panel works regardless of this setting.
Sandbox_ZT_ApiKey_tooltip: Server-only. WARNING: sandbox values replicate to all clients in MP. Whitelist-only servers only.
Sandbox_ZT_BrainMode_tooltip: Cognitive: full 18-module brain with Bayesian beliefs, goals, mood, bandit learning. Deterministic: legacy single-rule brain (fallback if cognitive misbehaves).
Sandbox_ZT_CycleSeconds_tooltip: Real-time seconds between Director decisions. Range 10-3600 (10s to 1 hour). Lower than 30 on Cognitive may cause plan churn; higher values (300+) give long peaceful stretches between events — pair with base-building runs.
Sandbox_ZT_DailyCallCap_tooltip: Hard limit on brain calls per real-world day. 0 disables the cap.
Sandbox_ZT_DashboardEnabled_tooltip: Writes a JSON snapshot of the brain to Zomboid/Lua/ZT_brain.json every 5 seconds, for the optional web dashboard.
Sandbox_ZT_DebugTeleportToSpawn_tooltip: When the Director spawns a horde, automatically teleport you to the spawn point. For testing only — disable for normal play.
Sandbox_ZT_DryRun_tooltip: Log every action the brain picks but do NOT execute it. Use to verify the director is making reasonable decisions before letting it loose.
Sandbox_ZT_Enabled_tooltip: Master switch. Off = director never ticks.
Sandbox_ZT_Model_tooltip: Default Sonnet. Haiku is cheapest, Opus is smartest.
Sandbox_ZT_MonologueRate_tooltip: How often the inner voice speaks. Sparse = only big moments, Chatty = ambient musings welcome.
Sandbox_ZT_VisualDebug_tooltip: Outline Director-spawned zombies in cyan and show a brief on-screen toast each time the Director acts. For testing only.
Sandbox_ZT_VoiceMode_tooltip: Off = silent. Director = the original menacing taunts. Monologue = your character thinks out loud, voice-flavored by their PZ traits + profession. Mutually exclusive.
Sandbox_ZT_VoiceProfile_tooltip: Force a specific monologue voice or let it be picked from your character's traits + profession. Auto picks once per character; force overrides without changing the cache.
Sandbox_ZenAnimals_DisableAttackIfStress: Animals will no longer attack players when stressed.
Sandbox_ZenAnimals_DisableCanDoLaceratio: Animals will no longer be able to cause laceration wounds on characters.
Sandbox_ZenAnimals_DisableKnockdownAttac: Animals will no longer be able to knock down characters with their attacks.
Sandbox_ZenAnimals_DisableStressAboveGro: Animals will no longer become stressed from being above ground.
Sandbox_ZenAnimals_DisableStressUnderRai: Animals will no longer become stressed when exposed to rain.
Sandbox_ZenAnimals_EnableZenGenome_toolt: When enabled, the stress gene range is locked to 0 so all newly spawned animals start genetically calm.
Sandbox_ZenAnimals_EnableZeroStress_tool: All animals inside animal zones will have 0 stress.
Sandbox_ZeroToChad_BraveKills_tooltip: Zombie kills needed to earn Brave.
Sandbox_ZeroToChad_CapPerStep_tooltip: Points per milestone, ONLY when Grant Desensitized is disabled.\nWith Desensitized enabled it is spread to reach 100 at its milestone.
Sandbox_ZeroToChad_CureClumsy_tooltip: The Clumsy trait is lost when reaching the Brave milestone.\nCombat experience steadies your feet.
Sandbox_ZeroToChad_DesensitizedKills_too: Zombie kills needed to earn Desensitized.
Sandbox_ZeroToChad_EnableBrave_tooltip: Grants Brave at its kill milestone.\nThat milestone also counts double toward the reduction, trait owned or not.
Sandbox_ZeroToChad_EnableDesensitized_to: Grants Desensitized at its milestone and removes the phobias.\nEnds the progression.
Sandbox_ZeroToChad_EnablePanicCap_toolti: Each milestone permanently lowers the character's maximum panic.\nDisable to keep only the trait milestones.
Sandbox_ZeroToChad_KillsPerStep_tooltip: Zombie kills needed for each milestone.
Sandbox_ZeroToChad_ShowNotifications_too: Shows a floating thought when a milestone is reached (at midnight).
Sandbox_ZevonArmorChain_tooltip: Sets the spawn rate of chainmail armor. (Found in anthropology, and fancy wardrobes)
Sandbox_ZevonArmsAncient_tooltip: Sets the spawn rate of ancient weapons: Khopesh, Gladius, Falx, etc.
Sandbox_ZevonArmsAsian_tooltip: Sets the spawn rate of asian weapons: Dao, Naginata, Jian, etc.
Sandbox_ZevonArmsEuro_tooltip: Sets the spawn rate of european weapons: Long Sword, Poleaxe, Mace, etc.
Sandbox_ZevonArmsExotic_tooltip: Sets the spawn rate of indigenous weapons: War Club, Bone Tomahawk, Macuahuitl, etc.
Sandbox_ZevonArmsModern_tooltip: Sets the spawn rate of 1800s enlightenment weapons: Sabre, Cutlass, Sawback Sword, etc.
Sandbox_ZllegroDailyPurchaseLimit: Shop: how many of one item per day
Sandbox_ZllegroDailyPurchaseLimit_toolti: The most units of a single catalogue item one player can buy in one in-game day. Counted per player and per item, so buying your fill of bandages does not limit buying chocolate. Resets each in-game day.
Sandbox_ZllegroDailySellLimit: Trade-in: how many of one item per day
Sandbox_ZllegroDailySellLimit_tooltip: The most units of a single item one player can sell back through the Scanner in one in-game day. Counted separately from the daily purchase limit -- buying and selling have their own independent caps.
Sandbox_ZllegroEconomyBaseHours: Economy delivery: hours until it arrives
Sandbox_ZllegroEconomyBaseHours_tooltip: How many in-game hours an Economy order takes to turn up, before the packing and rain delays. Economy is the slowest tier, meant to be the cheap and patient option.
Sandbox_ZllegroEconomyPriceMultiplier: Economy delivery: shipping fee (x goods value)
Sandbox_ZllegroEconomyPriceMultiplier_to: Shipping is charged ON TOP of the goods, priced as this multiple of the cart's value. 0 = free shipping, the cheapest the slow tier can be. 0.75 = you pay 1.75x in total. Set it below the Standard fee to make waiting longer genuinely worth it.
Sandbox_ZllegroExpressBaseHours: Express delivery: hours until it arrives
Sandbox_ZllegroExpressBaseHours_tooltip: How many in-game hours an Express order takes to turn up, before the per-item packing delay and any rain delay are added. Express is the fastest and most expensive of the three checkout tiers. Lower = faster.
Sandbox_ZllegroExpressPriceMultiplier: Express delivery: shipping fee (x goods value)
Sandbox_ZllegroExpressPriceMultiplier_to: Shipping is charged ON TOP of the goods, priced as this multiple of the cart's value. 0 = free shipping. 1.0 = shipping equals the goods' value, so you pay 2x in total. 2.5 = you pay 3.5x in total. Affects price only, never speed. Stacks with the night-order multiplier.
Sandbox_ZllegroMaxCartItemQuantity: Shop: largest quantity per cart line
Sandbox_ZllegroMaxCartItemQuantity_toolt: The most units of one item a player can put in a single cart line. This is only a per-order cap -- it does not change the daily purchase limit above.
Sandbox_ZllegroNightPriceMultiplier: Night orders: extra multiplier on the shipping fee
Sandbox_ZllegroNightPriceMultiplier_tool: Applied on top of the chosen tier's shipping fee for orders placed between 21:00 and 06:00. It multiplies the SHIPPING only, never the value of the goods themselves. Affects price only, never speed. Set to 1.0 to remove the night surcharge entirely.
Sandbox_ZllegroPerItemDelayHours: Packing time: extra hours per item
Sandbox_ZllegroPerItemDelayHours_tooltip: Extra delivery hours added for every single unit in the cart, on all three tiers. Ordering 5 bandages adds five times this. Makes big orders take proportionally longer. Set to 0 so order size never affects delivery time.
Sandbox_ZllegroRainDelayHoursMax_tooltip: Upper end of the extra delay added when an order is placed during heavy rain. Set equal to the minimum to make the rain delay fixed instead of random. Set both to 0 to switch rain delays off.
Sandbox_ZllegroRainDelayHoursMin_tooltip: Lower end of the extra delay added when an order is placed during heavy rain. One value is rolled between this and the maximum, and the same value is added to all three tiers. Set both to the same number for a fixed delay.
Sandbox_ZllegroRestockMaxDays_tooltip: Longest random wait, in in-game days, before a sold-out item comes back into stock. Each item rolls its own wait between the minimum and this, so they do not all restock together.
Sandbox_ZllegroRestockMinDays_tooltip: Shortest random wait, in in-game days, before a sold-out item comes back into stock. Only applies to items with no custom restock timer set in the in-game Admin Catalog; a per-item override always wins.
Sandbox_ZllegroRotationSlotCount: Stock rotation: how many slots in a cycle
Sandbox_ZllegroRotationSlotCount_tooltip: How many rotation slots the shop cycles through before repeating. Items can be limited to specific slots in the Admin Catalog, so more slots spreads limited-availability stock over a longer cycle.
Sandbox_ZllegroRotationSlotDays: Stock rotation: days spent on each slot
Sandbox_ZllegroRotationSlotDays_tooltip: How many in-game days the shop stays on one rotation slot before moving to the next. Multiply by the number of slots for the full cycle length: 5 slots x 7 days = 35 days before slot-limited items come round again.
Sandbox_ZllegroSellFollowsRotation: Trade-in: shop only buys in-season items
Sandbox_ZllegroSellFollowsRotation_toolt: When ON, the Scanner only buys an item back during the rotation weeks it is in stock for -- the shop pays for what it is currently trading, so players hold loot until its week comes round. When OFF (the default) the Scanner buys any catalogued item at any time, which is how Z-llegro has always behaved. Turning this on with the default catalog is strict: most items sit in a single rotation slot, so they are only bought one week in five. Best paired with a catalog whose items span two or more weeks.
Sandbox_ZllegroSellOnlyDailyLimit: Trade-in: daily limit for sell-only items
Sandbox_ZllegroSellOnlyDailyLimit_toolti: Sell-only items are ones players can sell in but nobody can buy -- they exist to give low-demand loot (jewellery, trinkets) a cash value without flooding the shop. Because nothing ever removes them from circulation, they get their own tighter daily cap instead of the normal trade-in limit. Counted per player, per item, per in-game day. Raise it if you want sell-only items to be a serious money sink.
Sandbox_ZllegroSellPricePercent: Trade-in: payout as %% of buy price
Sandbox_ZllegroSellPricePercent_tooltip: What percentage of an item's current shop price the Scanner pays when a player sells it back. 40 means selling back returns 40%% of what buying it costs. Uses the live price, so re-pricing an item changes its payout too.
Sandbox_ZllegroStandardBaseHours: Standard delivery: hours until it arrives
Sandbox_ZllegroStandardBaseHours_tooltip: How many in-game hours a Standard order takes to turn up, before the packing and rain delays. Standard is the middle tier -- slower than Express, cheaper than it.
Sandbox_ZllegroStandardPriceMultiplier: Standard delivery: shipping fee (x goods value)
Sandbox_ZllegroStandardPriceMultiplier_t: Shipping is charged ON TOP of the goods, priced as this multiple of the cart's value. 0 = free shipping. 0.5 = shipping costs half what the goods are worth (1.5x total). 1.0 = shipping equals the goods' value (2x total). Affects price only, never speed.
Sandbox_ZllegroStockFloodMultiplier_tool: Selling items back adds them to the shop's stock, which can push it past the item's normal maximum. This caps how far: stock can never exceed the item's max multiplied by this number, so players cannot flood the shop.
Sandbox_ZombieCoreDropChance_tooltip: Percentage chance for zombies to drop Strange Zombie Core (1-100%%).
Sandbox_ZombieDensityCellRadius_tooltip: How many cells around the player to scan and draw on the world map. 1 = 3x3 grid (cheap), 2 = 5x5 (default), 3 = 7x7 (most coverage, highest cost).
Sandbox_ZombieOnly_tooltip: Enable this if you want the Proximity Inventory to work only on zombies

Sandbox_disablePowerRequirement_tooltip: Disable the requirement for jukeboxes to have a supply of electricity; the power of music will be sufficient to keep a jukebox alive.
Sandbox_enableJukeboxNutrition_tooltip: Jukebox music can be food for both the soul AND the body! If you enable this feature, players will gain nutrition when they hear a track begin in a jukebox. The amount of nutrition gained per track is determined by the settings on this page. This setting applies the same exploit prevention strategies that are used for Jukebox Therapy.
Sandbox_enableJukeboxTherapy_tooltip: Give your music a degree in psychology! If you enable this feature, players will recover in a variety of ways whenever a True Music track begins in an audible jukebox. This feature is designed to prevent exploitation; players cannot benefit repeatedly by rapidly skipping tracks or playing 20 jukeboxes at a time. Reduction values below are normalized on a scale from 0 to 100 percent reduction (relative to the maximum value a state can take).
Sandbox_enableLifestyleFavoriteEffects_t: If Lifestyle is installed on your server and this feature is enabled, players who are dancing to the music of at least one audible jukebox will benefit from Lifestyle moodle effects as though they are hearing their favorite music played by an expert. This effect only occurs while they dance in order to circumvent a possible conflict between the availability of Lifestyle's normal Dance option and the availability of our version.
Sandbox_enableLifestyleIntegrations_tool: If Lifestyle is installed on your server and this feature is enabled, Lifestyle tracks will mute True Music Jukebox tracks, and our tracks will mute their tracks. You will also be able to trigger random styles of Lifestyle dancing whenever Lifestyle's built-in dance option is unavailable in the context menu.
Sandbox_enableStaticPlayerHealth_tooltip: Enable this setting in order to ensure that player weights will not change from day to day, regardless of nutrition. Additionally, players will recover healthy levels of calories, carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids every day. The purpose of this setting is to promote endless partying without fear of death by starvation; it does not stop zombies from eating people.
Sandbox_fallChance_Name_tooltip: How much a someone with the football player perk multiplies the reduction of the chance of being tripped.
Sandbox_footballObject_Name_tooltip: Decides how much holding a football contributes to being able to push over a zomboid (via addition and can be in either the primary or secondary slot).
Sandbox_forceThreeDimensionalAudio_toolt: Forces all players on the server to use Project Zomboid's 3D sound mode, which causes sound to be impacted by rooms and walls. We think this makes the music sound worse in a lot of cases, so we recommend leaving this off and allowing your players to choose their own sound mode on an individual basis using their in-game Mod Options. By default, this mod uses its own custom 3D sound mode.
Sandbox_headOnAmount_Name_tooltip: Adjusts how directly you must be moving toward a zomboid to trigger a tackle (0 means any direction, while 1 would mean directly infront of you, with the cone of influence getting bigger as the number decreases).
Sandbox_heroStarterTracks_tooltip: How many random cassettes and vinyls should a jukebox hero gain at character creation? <RGB:1.0,0.6,0.0>
Sandbox_ignoreDistanceWhenPlaying_toolti: If this option is enabled, songs will begin no matter how far players are from their source in order to maximize sync between all clients at all times. However, due to how Zomboid handles the creation of sound, clients may briefly stutter when songs start. If you disable this option, clients will not be in sync until they are within range of a jukebox while it is changing tracks, but they will not play tracks that are not audible to them, reducing the frequency of this stutter.

"(NOT YET IMPLEMENTED) Cooldown Reduction = Cooldown duration * AimSkillReductionMultiplier * (AimingSkill/10)"
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankBonusDama: Point Blank - Bonus Damage Multiplier (ONLY USED WHEN InstantKill is DISABLED)

This multiplier is applied to your bonus damage from above. This does NOT affect BASE damage value, ONLY bonus damage. See equation below: 

 TotalDamage = BaseDamage + PointBlankDamage
 PointBlankDamage = (Max(BaseDamage,PointBlankMinimumBonusDamage) * PointBlankBonusDamageMultiplier )
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankCooldownD: Point Blank - Cooldown Between Point Blank Kills at Min Aiming Skill (seconds)

Real-world seconds required between point blank triggers at Aiming skill level 0, regardless of game speed or framerate. This is the longest the cooldown gets - it scales down toward PointBlankCooldownDurationMin as Aiming skill increases.
Point Blank - Cooldown Between Point Blank Kills at Max Aiming Skill (seconds)

The cooldown used once the player has reached Aiming skill level 10. This is the shortest the cooldown gets - it scales linearly between this and PointBlankCooldownDurationMax based on the player's current Aiming skill level.
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankDisableMu: Point Blank - Disable Multiplayer Command Updates

For debugging purposes. You shouldn't change this. But if you're having server/client/networking issues, this will disable synchronous server/client updates. Without this, when you pointblank kill a zed, there can be a delay for them to appear dead for other players.
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankEffective: Same as Point Blank Effective Range, but for two-handed weapons (rifles, shotguns). Set higher than the value above, since the muzzle sits further from the player's body.
Zombies shot at a distance below this value will take point blank damage. Applies to one-handed weapons (pistols, revolvers).
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankExperimen: Limits one trigger pull to a single point blank victim. Point Blank resolves its kill before the engine picks what the bullet hits, so the engine skips the already-dead zombie and the shot can no longer put down a second one out of your line of fire. Turn this off to restore the previous behaviour.
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankInstantKi:
If TRUE, when shooting a zombie within point blank range, they die instantly. 
 If FALSE, the values below help determine bonus damage
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankMinTicksB: Point Blank - Min Ticks Between Point Blank Kills
You can set this higher to enforce a "cooldown" between point blank kills. By default, this ensures point blank can't trigger multiple times in a single tick
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankMinimumBo: Point Blank - Minimum Bonus Damage (ONLY USED WHEN InstantKill is DISABLED)

The minimum amount of bonus damage applied when InstantKill is disabled. 
For example, if your base damage is .0001, this raises the effective bonus damage to at least this value (default .15). 
 See equation below: 

 TotalDamage = BaseDamage + PointBlankDamage
 PointBlankDamage = (Max(BaseDamage,PointBlankMinimumBonusDamage) * PointBlankBonusDamageMultiplier )
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankUseExperi: If true, hit detection is much more lenient. Movement and aim duration no longer matter - zombies within range will die (or take point blank damage) regardless.
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankXpMultipl: Any xp gains from killing a zombie will be multiplied by this value

Sandbox_zReV2_AntibodyPower2_tooltip:
Affects how quickly resistant antibodies eliminate the zombie virus from the body after activation in the stage.
-This trait is acquired by injecting the level 4 vaccine;
-If potency = 6, then ~5%% infection is removed per hour;
-If potency = 12, then ~10%% infection is removed per hour;
-If potency = 24, then ~20%% infection is removed per hour.
Sandbox_zReV2_AntibodyPower_tooltip:
Affects at which infection stage the resistant antibodies activate.
-This trait is acquired by injecting the level 4 vaccine;
-TERMINAL - when infected over 80%%, health drains, high chance of death;
-PRETERMINAL - when infected over 60%% (nausea, fever)(RECOMMENDED!);
-MODERATE - when infected over 40%% (mild nausea);
-INITIAL - when infected over 20%% (no symptoms).
Sandbox_zReV2_BookInWorldSpawnChance_too:

-This option affects the drop chance in SPECIAL ZOMBIES.
Sandbox_zReV2_ResearchMinHealthNotificat:
Affects at what health level the character will notify
about crossing the critical health threshold specified in this parameter!
Sandbox_zReV2_ResearchRand_tooltip:
Only works for the vaccine improvement research type "PROGRESSIVE CHANCE" and "FULL RESEARCH"!
-In case of failed research, increases the result by a randomizer depending on this number (hereafter referred to as X);
-The formula works as:
Rand(X, X*2) for research up to level 2;
Rand(X*0.75, X*1.5) for research up to level 3;
Rand(X*0.5, X) for research up to level 4!
-Rounded up to the nearest whole number;
-Simply put: the randomizer decreases for researching a new vaccine by ~30%% on average.
Sandbox_zReV2_ResearchReduceHealth_toolt: When performing the recipe "Take blood for further work" your health will be reduced by this value!
Sandbox_zReV2_ResearchType_tooltip:
Choice of result type for improving (researching) new vaccine levels.
-PROGRESSIVE CHANCE - on failure, the next success chance increases (accumulates);
-STATIC CHANCE - fixed percentage chance of success (30,20,14%% from second to fourth);
-FULL RESEARCH - there is a hidden progress bar for study (100 units, conditionally, each research fills the bar).
